tm.m: Intrapartum gonococcal inoculation causes hyperacute purulent keratitis that can perforate intact cornea
tm.g: Hyperacute profuse purulent conjunctivitis in the first 48 hours of life -> Neisseria gonorrhoeae
f: watery discharge and a tender preauricular node after an upper respiratory infection
mucopurulent conjunctivitis beginning at 8 days of life with patchy pneumonitis
unilateral watery overflow with a white conjunctiva from 3 weeks of age
periocular clustered vesicles and a branching dendritic corneal ulcer at 10 days old
x: Adenoviral conjunctivitis presents later with watery discharge and preauricular lymphadenopathy rather than hyperacute neonatal pus.
Chlamydial ophthalmia neonatorum has a longer incubation period and typically presents between days 5 and 14 of life.
Congenital nasolacrimal duct obstruction causes a chronic watery eye with mild sticky reflux on lacrimal sac pressure and an uninflamed white conjunctiva.
Neonatal herpes simplex conjunctivitis usually presents at 1 to 2 weeks with periocular vesicles and dendritic corneal ulceration.

hq_q.s:
A 26 year old woman who wears monthly soft contact lenses has had a red, painful left eye for 1 day. Her vision in that eye is blurred and bright light hurts.
Visual acuity is 6/18 in the left eye and 6/6 in the right. The left eye is red around the cornea. Fluorescein shows a small corneal defect with a white opacity.
hq_q.w: Contact lens users with pain risk keratitis from Pseudomonas or Acanthamoeba. They need same-day review.
hq_q.f: A non-contact lens user with sticky eyes and no pain → conjunctivitis.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most appropriate next step?

tm.m: Lens wear lets bacteria or Acanthamoeba invade the cornea; ulcers can perforate in days
tm.g: Contact lens wearer with pain and a corneal opacity: same-day eye referral
f: the presentation instead showed features specific to Chloramphenicol drops (Chloramphenicol is not enough for a contact lens ulcer, which risks Pseudomonas or Acanthamoeba)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Lubricant drops (Lubricants do not treat a corneal infection)

the presentation instead showed features specific to Ofloxacin drops and GP review (A quinolone is the right class, but a lens wearer with a corneal opacity needs scrapes for culture (including Acanthamoeba) by eye casualty before treatment starts)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Review in 3 days (Delays sight-saving treatment for suspected microbial keratitis)
x: Chloramphenicol is not enough for a contact lens ulcer, which risks Pseudomonas or Acanthamoeba.
Lubricants do not treat a corneal infection.
A quinolone is the right class, but a lens wearer with a corneal opacity needs scrapes for culture (including Acanthamoeba) by eye casualty before treatment starts.
Delays sight-saving treatment for suspected microbial keratitis

hq_q.s:
A 6 year old girl has had red, gritty eyes that are stuck together with crusting on waking for the past 2 days. She is afebrile, systemically well, and has normal vision.
On examination, both conjunctivae show diffuse tarsal injection with mucopurulent discharge, clear corneas, and briskly reactive pupils. Her mother asks about school attendance.
o: She can stay at school without exclusion
When the conjunctivae are completely white
hq_q.w: UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) guidance states that children with simple acute infective conjunctivitis do not require exclusion from school or nursery, unless there is a widespread institutional outbreak.
hq_q.f: An outbreak in the class → speak to the health protection team.
hq_q.ql: When can she return to school?

tm.m: Simple infective conjunctivitis is self-limiting and routine school exclusion does not prevent transmission
tm.g: Uncomplicated infective conjunctivitis in a well child -> no school exclusion required
f: chickenpox with new vesicular lesions still cropping within the past 5 days
impetigo treated with topical or oral antibiotics before lesions have crusted over
neonatal purulent conjunctivitis within the first 28 days of life requiring urgent swabs
an adenovirus outbreak where the nursery has been advised to restrict symptomatic contacts
x: A week of isolation is unnecessary for uncomplicated conjunctivitis under UKHSA public health rules.
UKHSA guidance does not require starting or completing 48 hours of topical antibiotics before attending school.
Routine microbiological swabs and clearance testing are not indicated in uncomplicated childhood conjunctivitis.
Waiting for complete resolution of conjunctival injection needlessly keeps well children out of school.

hq_q.s:
A 38 year old man has had a painful, red, watery right eye for 2 weeks. He had a cold sore before it started. His GP started eye drops 5 days ago, and since then the pain and blurring have got worse.
Visual acuity is 6/24 in the right eye. Fluorescein shows a large corneal ulcer with broad, map-like, branching edges.
hq_q.w: Topical steroids boost herpes simplex replication and turn a dendritic ulcer into a large geographic ulcer. They are not used in active epithelial herpes keratitis; treatment is topical aciclovir or ganciclovir.
hq_q.f: Same ulcer while using aciclovir ointment → that is the correct treatment, not the cause.
hq_q.ql: Which drop is most likely to have made it worse?

tm.m: Steroids suppress local immunity, so the herpes virus spreads across the corneal epithelium
tm.g: Herpetic ulcer getting worse on drops: think steroid
f: the presentation instead showed features specific to Chloramphenicol (Chloramphenicol does not treat herpes, but it does not make the ulcer spread; it is often given harmlessly for a presumed bacterial red eye)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Cyclopentolate (Cyclopentolate dilates the pupil and eases ciliary spasm; it does not feed viral spread)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Fusidic acid (Fusidic acid is an anti-staphylococcal antibiotic with no effect on herpes replication)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Hypromellose (Hypromellose is an inert lubricant; it soothes but does not worsen the ulcer)
x: Chloramphenicol does not treat herpes, but it does not make the ulcer spread; it is often given harmlessly for a presumed bacterial red eye.
Cyclopentolate dilates the pupil and eases ciliary spasm; it does not feed viral spread.
Fusidic acid is an anti-staphylococcal antibiotic with no effect on herpes replication.

hq_q.f: A contact lens wearer with a white spot and pus → Pseudomonas.
hq_q.ql: Which organism is most likely?

tm.m: Acanthamoeba from water invades the cornea and nerves, causing severe pain
tm.g: A ring infiltrate with severe pain after tap water exposure is Acanthamoeba
f: Chlamydia trachomatis
a branching dendritic ulcer after a cold sore

hq_q.s:
A 68 year old woman has had a painful blistering rash on the right side of her forehead for 2 days.
There are grouped vesicles on an erythematous base over the right forehead and upper eyelid, and vesicles on the tip of the nose. The right eye is slightly red. Visual acuity is 6/6.
hq_q.w: Vesicles on the side or tip of the nose in herpes zoster ophthalmicus (Hutchinson's sign) indicate involvement of the nasociliary branch of the ophthalmic nerve (V1), which also innervates the cornea and uvea.
hq_q.f: Shingles on the forehead without nose tip → still refer if eye symptoms.
hq_q.ql: Which complication is she most at risk of?

c: vesicles on the tip of the nose
tm.m: The nasociliary branch of V1 innervates both the nasal tip skin and the anterior globe
tm.g: Herpes zoster ophthalmicus with nasal tip vesicles (Hutchinson's sign) -> ocular involvement

hq_q.s:
A 28 year old man has had a painful red right eye and blurred vision for 2 days. Bright light makes the pain worse. He has had back stiffness in the mornings for a year that improves with exercise.
Visual acuity is 6/12 in the right eye. There is redness around the cornea. The right pupil is small and irregular. There is no discharge.
hq_q.w: Acute anterior uveitis (iritis) is strongly associated with HLA-B27 spondyloarthropathies such as ankylosing spondylitis. Ciliary spasm and posterior synechiae between the inflamed iris and lens cause photophobia, circumcorneal redness, and a small irregular pupil.
hq_q.f: A mid-dilated pupil and haloes → acute glaucoma.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most likely diagnosis?

c: Bright light makes the pain worse
tm.m: HLA-B27 autoimmune inflammation targets the iris and ciliary body, forming posterior synechiae
tm.g: Painful photophobic red eye with small irregular pupil and inflammatory back pain -> anterior uveitis

mucopurulent discharge sticking the lashes together with normal vision and reactive pupils

hq_q.s:
A 34 year old woman with Crohn's disease presents to eye casualty with a 3 day history of a painful, red, photophobic left eye and mildly blurred vision.
Visual acuity is 6/12 on the left. Slit-lamp examination shows circumcorneal injection and inflammatory cells and flare in the anterior chamber. Intraocular pressure is 14 mmHg and fluorescein staining shows no corneal ulceration.
hq_q.w: Confirmed non-infectious acute anterior uveitis is treated with intensive topical corticosteroid drops (such as prednisolone acetate) to suppress intraocular inflammation and cycloplegic mydriatic drops (such as cyclopentolate) to relieve ciliary spasm and break posterior synechiae.
hq_q.f: Acute glaucoma → pilocarpine.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most appropriate treatment?

tm.m: Topical corticosteroids suppress uveal inflammation while cycloplegics paralyse the ciliary body and prevent synechiae
tm.g: Non-infectious anterior uveitis on slit lamp -> topical steroid and cycloplegic dilating drops

tm.g: ANA-positive oligoarticular JIA: regular slit-lamp checks

hq_q.s:
A 35 year old man has had a red patch in his left eye for 2 days. It feels mildly uncomfortable, but his vision is 6/6 and he has no discharge or photophobia.
Examination shows a localized sectoral leash of dilated vessels on the temporal globe. The vessels move freely over the underlying sclera with a cotton bud and blanch rapidly after topical 2.5% phenylephrine drops.
hq_q.w: Episcleritis causes benign, self-limiting inflammation of the superficial episcleral plexus. Unlike deep scleral vessels in scleritis, episcleral vessels are mobile over the globe and blanch promptly with topical phenylephrine.
hq_q.f: Severe pain at night with a bluish tinge → scleritis.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most likely diagnosis?

c: move freely over the underlying sclera
tm.m: Superficial episcleral plexus vessels are mobile and constrict in response to topical phenylephrine
tm.g: Mild sectoral redness with mobile vessels that blanch with phenylephrine -> episcleritis
f: severe ocular pain, haloes, a hazy cornea and a fixed mid-dilated pupil

A 6 year old girl has had a red, swollen left upper eyelid for 1 day after a scratch from her cat.
Temperature 37.8°C. The left upper lid is red and swollen. She can open her eye. Eye movements are full and painless, there is no proptosis and visual acuity is 6/6 in both eyes.

hq_q.f: Painful eye movements and proptosis → orbital cellulitis.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most likely diagnosis?

tm.m: Infection in front of the orbital septum spares the eye and its muscles
tm.g: Swollen lid with full painless movements, normal vision and no proptosis is periorbital cellulitis

hq_q.f: Abscess on CT → surgical drainage with IV antibiotics.

tm.m: Sinus infection spreads behind the septum; CT shows abscesses and spread
tm.g: Suspected orbital cellulitis: CT orbit and sinuses

hq_q.f: Fever with neck stiffness and no eye spread → meningitis.

c: right eye has also become swollen

tm.g: Spread to the other eye with ophthalmoplegia is cavernous sinus thrombosis

A 58 year old man has noticed a dark shadow spreading across the vision of his right eye since this morning. Two days ago he saw flashing lights and many new floaters. He is short-sighted. There is no pain.
Visual acuity is 6/12 in the right eye. There is a superior field defect on confrontation.
hq_q.w: Posterior vitreous detachment in a myopic eye can tear the peripheral retina, allowing liquefied vitreous to track beneath the neurosensory retina. Photopsia and a shower of floaters followed by a spreading curtain-like field defect require same-day ophthalmic surgical assessment.
hq_q.f: Sudden floaters with no shadow → posterior vitreous detachment.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most likely diagnosis?

c: flashing lights and many new floaters

tm.g: Photopsia and new floaters followed by a progressive curtain field defect -> retinal detachment

A 54 year old myopic woman presents to eye casualty after noticing flashing lights and floaters followed by a dark curtain in the lower field of her left eye this morning.
Visual acuity is 6/6 in both eyes. Dilated fundoscopy reveals a superior rhegmatogenous retinal detachment with a horseshoe tear that has not yet reached the macula.
hq_q.w: A macula-on retinal detachment (where central visual acuity is still preserved and the fovea remains attached) is an ophthalmic emergency requiring vitreoretinal repair within 24 hours before subretinal fluid detaches the macula and permanently impairs central acuity.
hq_q.f: Macula-off → still urgent, but less time-critical.

tm.g: Macula-on retinal detachment with preserved central acuity -> vitreoretinal surgery within 24 hours

Even a few days of delay in a superior macula-on detachment allows fluid to progress across the fovea.
A 6 month delay guarantees irreversible photoreceptor death and loss of sight in the affected eye.

A 60 year old woman has had new floaters and flashing lights in her left eye for 2 days. She has no shadow or curtain over her vision. She is not short-sighted.

hq_q.s:
A 68 year old man had sudden painless loss of vision in his left eye yesterday, like a curtain coming down. It lasted 5 minutes and recovered completely. He has hypertension and smokes. He has no headache, jaw pain or scalp tenderness. He has started aspirin.
Visual acuity is 6/6 in both eyes. Fundoscopy is normal. There is a bruit over the left carotid artery.
hq_q.w: Amaurosis fugax is a TIA of the retina, usually from an embolus from the carotid bifurcation. Carotid imaging finds a stenosis that may need endarterectomy within 2 weeks to prevent a stroke.
hq_q.f: Same episode with headache, jaw pain and a raised ESR → giant cell arteritis; steroids the same day.
hq_q.ql: Which investigation is most important?

c: bruit over the left carotid artery
tm.m: Cholesterol or platelet emboli from a carotid plaque block the retinal artery for minutes
tm.g: Amaurosis fugax: image the carotids
f: the presentation instead showed features specific to CT head (Brain imaging may be done in the TIA clinic, but the key test is the carotid, the usual source of the embolus)
the presentation instead showed features specific to ESR and CRP (These are urgent if giant cell arteritis is possible, but he has no headache, jaw pain or scalp tenderness and has a carotid bruit)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Formal visual field testing (His vision has fully recovered, so fields will be normal and do not find the cause)
the presentation instead showed features specific to MRI of the orbits (Orbital MRI looks for optic nerve disease, which does not cause brief curtain-like loss)
x: Brain imaging may be done in the TIA clinic, but the key test is the carotid, the usual source of the embolus.
These are urgent if giant cell arteritis is possible, but he has no headache, jaw pain or scalp tenderness and has a carotid bruit.
His vision has fully recovered, so fields will be normal and do not find the cause.
Orbital MRI looks for optic nerve disease, which does not cause brief curtain-like loss.

hq_q.s:
A 76 year old man had cataract surgery on his right eye 3 days ago. Since yesterday the eye has become increasingly painful and red and his vision has worsened.
Visual acuity is hand movements in the right eye. The eye is very red with lid swelling. There is a fluid level of pus in the anterior chamber.
hq_q.w: Infection after surgery is an emergency needing same-day review. Key discriminator: A painful red eye with hypopyon days after surgery is endophthalmitis.
hq_q.f: Gradual blurring months later → posterior capsule opacification.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most likely diagnosis?

c: cataract surgery on his right eye 3 days ago
tm.m: Bacteria enter during surgery and infect the inside of the eye
tm.g: A painful red eye with hypopyon days after surgery is endophthalmitis
f: the presentation instead showed features specific to Acute glaucoma (Angle closure does not cause pus in the anterior chamber days after surgery)
gritty eyes worse at the end of the day with no lid crusting
gradual blurring months later with a white eye
the presentation instead showed features specific to Retinal detachment (Detachment is painless; a painful red eye with falling vision after surgery is infection)
x: Angle closure does not cause pus in the anterior chamber days after surgery.
Ruled out here: requires gritty eyes worse at the end of the day with no lid crusting, whereas this patient has cataract surgery on his right eye 3 days ago, fluid level of pus.
Ruled out here: requires gradual blurring months later with a white eye, whereas this patient has cataract surgery on his right eye 3 days ago, fluid level of pus.
Detachment is painless; a painful red eye with falling vision after surgery is infection.

hq_q.s:
A 72 year old woman had uncomplicated cataract surgery on her left eye a year ago, after which her vision was excellent. Over the last few months her vision in that eye has gradually become blurred and she has glare from headlights.
Visual acuity is 6/18 in the left eye. The eye is white and painless. There is a hazy membrane behind the lens implant.
hq_q.w: The lens capsule clouds over months. YAG laser capsulotomy restores vision. Key discriminator: Gradual blur months after cataract surgery with a hazy capsule is capsule opacification.
hq_q.f: Sudden loss with floaters → retinal detachment.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most likely cause?

c: hazy membrane behind the lens implant
tm.m: Leftover lens cells grow over the capsule behind the implant
tm.g: Gradual blur months after cataract surgery with a hazy capsule is capsule opacification
f: the presentation instead showed features specific to Glaucoma (Glaucoma takes peripheral vision, not causing slow blur after previously excellent vision post-surgery)
Dry is slow and has drusen; wet is fast and needs injections.
the presentation instead showed features specific to Recurrent cataract (The natural lens was removed at surgery so a true cataract cannot recur)
a sudden shadow with floaters
x: Glaucoma takes peripheral vision, not causing slow blur after previously excellent vision post-surgery.
Ruled out here: requires Dry is slow and has drusen; wet is fast and needs injections, whereas this patient has a year ago, gradually become blurred.
The natural lens was removed at surgery so a true cataract cannot recur
Ruled out here: requires a sudden shadow with floaters, whereas this patient has a year ago, gradually become blurred.

hq_q.s:
A 6 week old baby girl has a white reflection in her right pupil on a flash photograph taken by her parents. The left eye looks normal in photos. She feeds well.
The red reflex is absent in the right eye and normal in the left.
hq_q.w: Leukocoria can mean retinoblastoma, which can be life-threatening. Refer urgently. Key discriminator: Leukocoria in a baby: exclude retinoblastoma.
hq_q.f: A cloudy lens since birth → congenital cataract.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most important diagnosis to exclude?

c: white reflection in her right pupil
red reflex is absent in the right eye
tm.m: A tumour or opacity behind the pupil blocks the red reflex
tm.g: Leukocoria in a baby: exclude retinoblastoma
f: the presentation instead showed features specific to Coloboma (A coloboma is a keyhole-shaped pupil present from birth, not a white reflex)
a cloudy lens seen since birth
the presentation instead showed features specific to Glaucoma (Congenital glaucoma gives a large, cloudy cornea and watering, not a white pupillary reflex)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Squint (A squint can be a sign of retinoblastoma, but the absent red reflex is what must be urgently explained)
x: A coloboma is a keyhole-shaped pupil present from birth, not a white reflex.
Ruled out here: requires a cloudy lens seen since birth, whereas this patient has white reflection in her right pupil, red reflex is absent in the right eye.
Congenital glaucoma gives a large, cloudy cornea and watering, not a white pupillary reflex.
A squint can be a sign of retinoblastoma, but the absent red reflex is what must be urgently explained.

hq_q.s:
A 78 year old woman has noticed that straight lines look wavy in her right eye for 2 weeks. Her central vision has become blurred.
Visual acuity is 6/24 in the right eye. Optical coherence tomography shows fluid beneath the macula with a choroidal neovascular membrane. She is diagnosed with wet macular degeneration.
hq_q.w: Injections into the eye of anti-VEGF drugs such as aflibercept stop new vessel growth. Key discriminator: Wet macular degeneration: anti-VEGF injections.
hq_q.f: Dry macular degeneration → no curative treatment, low vision support.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most appropriate treatment?

tm.m: VEGF drives leaky new vessels under the macula
tm.g: Wet macular degeneration: anti-VEGF injections
f: the presentation instead showed features specific to High-dose vitamins (Vitamins may slow dry AMD in some people but do not treat leaking new vessels)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Laser photocoagulation (Laser is for proliferative diabetic retinopathy; wet macular degeneration is treated with anti-VEGF injections)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Steroid drops (Risks raised intraocular pressure, cataract and corneal thinning in primary care)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Vitrectomy (Vitrectomy treats retinal detachment or vitreous haemorrhage, not wet macular degeneration)
x: Vitamins may slow dry AMD in some people but do not treat leaking new vessels.
Laser is for proliferative diabetic retinopathy; wet macular degeneration is treated with anti-VEGF injections.
Risks raised intraocular pressure, cataract and corneal thinning in primary care
Vitrectomy treats retinal detachment or vitreous haemorrhage, not wet macular degeneration.

hq_q.s: A 74 year old woman has gradual central blurring of vision in both eyes. Fundoscopy shows drusen and pigment changes at both maculae with no fluid or haemorrhage. She is diagnosed with dry macular degeneration. She smokes 15 cigarettes a day.
hq_q.w: Smoking is the main modifiable risk. Diet and supplements may slow progression. Key discriminator: Dry AMD in a smoker: stop smoking.
hq_q.f: Distortion appears suddenly → refer as wet AMD.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most appropriate advice?

tm.m: Smoking speeds macular degeneration; dry AMD has no injection treatment
tm.g: Dry AMD in a smoker: stop smoking
f: sudden distortion with fluid on OCT
the presentation instead showed features specific to Avoid reading (Visual tasks do not accelerate macular degeneration and low-vision aids should be encouraged)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Laser to the drusen (Laser to drusen does not slow dry AMD, and NICE advises against it)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Photodynamic therapy (Photodynamic therapy targets abnormal new vessels in some wet AMD; dry AMD has no new vessels to treat)
x: Ruled out here: requires sudden distortion with fluid on OCT, whereas this patient has drusen, no fluid or haemorrhage.
Visual tasks do not accelerate macular degeneration and low-vision aids should be encouraged
Laser to drusen does not slow dry AMD, and NICE advises against it.
Photodynamic therapy targets abnormal new vessels in some wet AMD; dry AMD has no new vessels to treat.

hq_q.s: A 72 year old man has wet macular degeneration in his left eye, which is being treated. His right eye has dry macular degeneration. He asks how he can check his right eye at home for signs that it has turned wet.
hq_q.w: Lines on an Amsler grid look bent in macular disease. Key discriminator: An Amsler grid detects central distortion.
hq_q.f: Colour vision loss → test with Ishihara plates.
hq_q.ql: Which test best detects new central distortion at home?

c: check his right eye at home
tm.m: Macular fluid bends straight lines
tm.g: An Amsler grid detects central distortion
f: testing colour vision
the presentation instead showed features specific to Pinhole test (A pinhole tests for refractive error, not macular distortion)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Snellen chart (A Snellen chart measures acuity but misses early distortion)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Visual fields (Field testing finds peripheral loss; the Amsler grid detects new central distortion at home)
x: Ruled out here: requires testing colour vision, whereas this patient has check his right eye at home, new central distortion.
A pinhole tests for refractive error, not macular distortion.
A Snellen chart measures acuity but misses early distortion.
Field testing finds peripheral loss; the Amsler grid detects new central distortion at home.

hq_q.s:
A 64 year old woman with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes has had double vision and a drooping right eyelid since yesterday, with an ache above the eye.
There is right ptosis and the right eye rests down and out. The right pupil is equal in size to the left and reacts normally to light. Other cranial nerves are normal.
hq_q.w: Ischaemic microvascular third nerve palsy from diabetes or hypertension infarts the central somatic nerve trunk while sparing the superficial parasympathetic pupillomotor fibres, producing complete ptosis and a 'down and out' eye with a normal reactive pupil.
hq_q.f: A dilated pupil → compressive third nerve palsy, such as an aneurysm.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most likely cause?

tm.m: Vasa nervorum ischaemia affects the core of CN III while sparing outer pial parasympathetic fibres
tm.g: Complete third nerve palsy with spared reactive pupil in diabetes -> microvascular third nerve palsy
f: ipsilateral third nerve palsy accompanied by acute contralateral arm and leg weakness
fluctuating bilateral ptosis and diplopia that worsen markedly on sustained upward gaze in the evening
sudden thunderclap headache, bitemporal hemianopia and hypotension in a patient with a pituitary adenoma
acute painful third nerve palsy with a fixed dilated right pupil
x: A midbrain stroke affecting the third nerve nucleus or fascicle causes contralateral hemiparesis (Weber's syndrome) or ataxia.
Ocular myasthenia gravis causes fluctuating, fatigable ptosis and variable diplopia that does not follow a single nerve pattern.
Pituitary apoplexy presents with sudden thunderclap headache, bitemporal visual field loss, and multiple cavernous sinus palsies.
Extrinsic compression by a posterior communicating artery aneurysm compresses the superficial pupillomotor fibres first, causing a dilated unreactive pupil.

hq_q.s:
A 48 year old man has had headaches for 6 months. He has recently started bumping into people on both sides when walking through crowds.
Visual acuity is 6/9 in both eyes. Confrontation testing shows a bitemporal hemianopia. The rest of the neurological examination is normal.
hq_q.w: A pituitary tumour presses on the optic chiasm, affecting both temporal fields. Key discriminator: Bitemporal hemianopia is chiasmal compression by a pituitary tumour.
hq_q.f: A homonymous hemianopia → lesion behind the chiasm.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most likely cause?

c: bumping into people on both sides
tm.m: A tumour pressing up on the chiasm cuts the crossing nasal fibres
tm.g: Bitemporal hemianopia is chiasmal compression by a pituitary tumour
f: a homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing
the presentation instead showed features specific to Optic neuritis (Optic neuritis affects one eye with pain on movement, not loss of both outer fields over months)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Retinal detachment (A detachment affects one eye, not both temporal fields)
an upper homonymous quadrantanopia
x: Ruled out here: requires a homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing, whereas this patient has bumping into people on both sides, bitemporal hemianopia.
Optic neuritis affects one eye with pain on movement, not loss of both outer fields over months.
A detachment affects one eye, not both temporal fields.
Ruled out here: requires an upper homonymous quadrantanopia, whereas this patient has bumping into people on both sides, bitemporal hemianopia.

hq_q.s:
A 64 year old man has had a cough for 3 months, pain in his left shoulder radiating down the inner arm, and has lost 6 kg. He has smoked for 45 years.
There is mild left ptosis with a small left pupil. The left side of his face is dry to touch compared with the right. There is wasting of the small muscles of the left hand.
hq_q.w: A lung apex tumour can damage the sympathetic chain, causing Horner's syndrome. Do a chest X-ray.
hq_q.f: Horner's with neck pain after trauma → carotid dissection.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most likely cause?

c: pain in his left shoulder radiating down the inner arm
tm.m: A lung apex tumour invades the sympathetic chain and the T1 root
tm.g: Horner's with hand wasting in a smoker is a Pancoast tumour
f: the presentation instead showed features specific to Bell's palsy (Bell's palsy affects the face, not the eye with Horner's and arm pain)
Horner's with vertigo, dysphagia and crossed sensory loss
fatigable ptosis and double vision
ptosis with a down and out eye and a dilated pupil
x: Bell's palsy affects the face, not the eye with Horner's and arm pain.
Ruled out here: requires Horner's with vertigo, dysphagia and crossed sensory loss, whereas this patient has pain in his left shoulder radiating down the inner arm, smoked for 45 years.
Ruled out here: requires fatigable ptosis and double vision, whereas this patient has pain in his left shoulder radiating down the inner arm, smoked for 45 years.
Ruled out here: requires ptosis with a down and out eye and a dilated pupil, whereas this patient has pain in his left shoulder radiating down the inner arm, smoked for 45 years.

hq_q.s:
A 34 year old man was hammering metal on metal without goggles 2 hours ago when he felt something hit his right eye. It is now sore and his vision is blurred.
Visual acuity is 6/18 in the right eye. There is a tiny full-thickness wound in the cornea and the pupil is slightly irregular. No foreign body is seen on the surface.
hq_q.w: Hammering metal on metal fires high-speed fragments that can enter the eye through a tiny wound. CT finds a metal intraocular foreign body and is safe; it must be removed to prevent endophthalmitis and iron toxicity.
hq_q.f: Same injury but the cornea is intact with a surface fragment → remove it at the slit lamp.
hq_q.ql: Which investigation is most appropriate?

c: hammering metal on metal without goggles
tm.m: A metal fragment inside the eye causes infection and iron toxicity unless it is found and removed
tm.g: Hammering metal plus a penetrating eye wound: CT orbits
f: the presentation instead showed features specific to Contact B-scan ultrasound (Pressing a probe on an open globe can push the eye contents out; CT is safer and better at finding metal)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Corneal scrape for culture (A scrape is for infective keratitis, not a fresh penetrating injury)
the presentation instead showed features specific to MRI of the orbits (MRI is dangerous with a possible metal fragment because the magnet can move it inside the eye)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Tonometry of the right eye (Measuring pressure presses on an eye that may be open; it waits until the globe is shown to be intact)
x: Pressing a probe on an open globe can push the eye contents out; CT is safer and better at finding metal.
A scrape is for infective keratitis, not a fresh penetrating injury.
MRI is dangerous with a possible metal fragment because the magnet can move it inside the eye.
Measuring pressure presses on an eye that may be open; it waits until the globe is shown to be intact.

hq_q.s:
A 24 year old woman was hit in the right eye by a squash ball 4 hours ago. Her vision is blurred.
Visual acuity is 6/18 in the right eye. There is a 2 mm layer of blood in the lower anterior chamber in front of the iris. The globe is intact.
hq_q.w: Hyphaema needs eye review because the pressure can rise and bleeding can recur. Key discriminator: Blood layering in the anterior chamber after blunt trauma is hyphaema.
hq_q.f: Double vision on looking up after a punch → orbital floor fracture.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most likely diagnosis?

c: layer of blood in the lower anterior chamber
tm.m: Blunt force tears iris vessels, and blood settles in the front chamber
tm.g: Blood layering in the anterior chamber after blunt trauma is hyphaema
f: the presentation instead showed features specific to Corneal abrasion (An abrasion gives a scratchy watery eye with fluorescein uptake, not a layer of blood in the anterior chamber)
double vision on looking up after a punch
the presentation instead showed features specific to Retinal detachment (A detachment is painless with flashes and floaters, not a visible blood level)
a painless red patch on the white of the eye
x: An abrasion gives a scratchy watery eye with fluorescein uptake, not a layer of blood in the anterior chamber.
Ruled out here: requires double vision on looking up after a punch, whereas this patient has squash ball, layer of blood in the lower anterior chamber.
A detachment is painless with flashes and floaters, not a visible blood level.
Ruled out here: requires a painless red patch on the white of the eye, whereas this patient has squash ball, layer of blood in the lower anterior chamber.

hq_q.s:
A 26 year old man was punched in the right eye 3 hours ago. He has double vision when he looks up.
There is bruising and swelling around the right eye. He cannot elevate the right eye fully. There is numbness of the right cheek and upper lip. Visual acuity is 6/6.
hq_q.w: Inferior rectus gets trapped and the infraorbital nerve is damaged. Key discriminator: Restricted upgaze with cheek numbness after a punch is an orbital floor fracture.
hq_q.f: Flattened cheekbone and trismus → zygoma fracture.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most likely diagnosis?

c: double vision when he looks up
cannot elevate the right eye fully
tm.m: The thin orbital floor breaks, trapping inferior rectus and damaging the infraorbital nerve
tm.g: Restricted upgaze with cheek numbness after a punch is an orbital floor fracture
f: blood in the front chamber of the eye
the presentation instead showed features specific to Retinal detachment (A detachment does not limit eye movement or numb the cheek)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Third nerve palsy (A third nerve palsy causes ptosis and an eye down and out, not cheek numbness and trapped upgaze)
a flattened cheekbone with trismus
x: Ruled out here: requires blood in the front chamber of the eye, whereas this patient has double vision when he looks up, cannot elevate the right eye fully.
A detachment does not limit eye movement or numb the cheek.
A third nerve palsy causes ptosis and an eye down and out, not cheek numbness and trapped upgaze.
Ruled out here: requires a flattened cheekbone with trismus, whereas this patient has double vision when he looks up, cannot elevate the right eye fully.

hq_q.s:
A 27 year old man presents to his GP with a 3-week history of pale, greasy, foul-smelling stools that float, accompanied by abdominal bloating,sulphurous belching and excessive flatulence. Four weeks ago he went wild camping in North Wales and drank untreated water from a mountain stream. He has no rectal bleeding or fever.
Temperature 36.9°C, pulse rate 72 bpm. The abdomen is mildly distended and non-tender, and he has lost 3 kg.
hq_q.w: Giardia lamblia (Giardia duodenalis) is a flagellated protozoan acquired from drinking contaminated stream or backcountry water. Trophozoites adhere to the proximal small-intestinal brush border, causing prolonged non-bloody steatorrhoea, bloating, flatulence and weight loss. Oral metronidazole or tinidazole is first-line treatment.
hq_q.f: Bloody diarrhoea with a liver abscess → Entamoeba histolytica.
hq_q.ql: Which causative organism is most likely responsible?

c: untreated water from a mountain stream
tm.m: Pear-shaped binucleate Giardia trophozoites attach to duodenal and jejunal enterocytes via a ventral sucking disc, blunting microvilli and impairing fat absorption.
tm.g: Prolonged greasy non-bloody diarrhoea and bloating after drinking stream water -> Giardia lamblia
x: Campylobacter jejuni causes acute febrile bloody diarrhoea and severe cramping 2 to 5 days after eating undercooked poultry rather than 3 weeks of non-febrile steatorrhoea.
Cryptosporidium causes profuse watery (non-greasy) diarrhoea after swimming pool or farm animal exposure, with acid-fast oocysts on modified Ziehl-Neelsen staining.
Entamoeba histolytica invades the colonic mucosa, causing amoebic dysentery (bloody mucoid stools) and right lobe liver abscesses rather than small-bowel steatorrhoea.
Shigella sonnei invades the distal colon via faecal-oral person-to-person spread, causing acute febrile bloody dysentery with tenesmus.
f: he developed acute fever, severe abdominal cramps and bloody diarrhoea 3 days after eating undercooked barbecue poultry
he developed profuse watery diarrhoea after a public swimming pool outbreak and stool microscopy showed acid-fast oocysts
he returned from India with bloody mucoid stools, right upper quadrant pain, fever and a solitary liver abscess on ultrasound
an outbreak of acute febrile bloody mucoid diarrhoea and tenesmus occurred among children and staff at a day nursery

hq_q.s:
A 30 year old woman developed watery diarrhoea 3 days after arriving in Mexico on holiday. She has 5 loose stools a day with cramps. There is no blood and she has no fever.
Temperature 37.1°C, pulse rate 88 bpm. The abdomen is soft with mild generalised tenderness.
hq_q.w: Enterotoxigenic E. coli is the commonest cause of traveller's diarrhoea: watery, short-lived and treated with fluids.
hq_q.f: Bloody diarrhoea after a petting farm → E. coli O157.
hq_q.ql: Which organism is most likely?

tm.m: Enterotoxigenic E. coli toxins make the gut secrete water without invading
tm.g: Watery traveller's diarrhoea is usually ETEC
f: bloody diarrhoea after a petting farm
the presentation instead showed features specific to Salmonella enterica Typhi (Typhoid gives a rising fever and headache, often with constipation, not watery diarrhoea 3 days into a trip)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Shigella flexneri (Shigella causes bloody diarrhoea with fever)
profuse rice-water stools
x: Ruled out here: requires bloody diarrhoea after a petting farm, whereas this patient has 3 days after arriving in Mexico, watery diarrhoea.
Typhoid gives a rising fever and headache, often with constipation, not watery diarrhoea 3 days into a trip.
Shigella causes bloody diarrhoea with fever.
Ruled out here: requires profuse rice-water stools, whereas this patient has 3 days after arriving in Mexico, watery diarrhoea.

hq_q.s:
A 34 year old restaurant sous-chef developed sudden-onset projectile vomiting and watery non-bloody diarrhoea 3 days ago, alongside several kitchen staff and diners. Stool PCR testing confirms norovirus infection. His last episode of diarrhoea or vomiting was 24 hours ago, and today he feels well and is eating normally.
Temperature 36.6°C, pulse rate 70 bpm. He attends occupational health regarding his return to kitchen duties.
o: 05 days after diarrhoea and vomiting have stopped
24 hours after diarrhoea and vomiting have stopped
48 hours after diarrhoea and vomiting have stopped
After 2 negative stool PCR samples taken 24 hours apart
Immediately if symptom-free for 12 hours and wearing gloves
hq_q.w: Under UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) and Food Standards Agency guidance, food handlers and healthcare staff with viral gastroenteritis (such as norovirus) must be excluded from work until they have been completely free of diarrhoea and vomiting for at least 48 hours.
hq_q.f: E. coli O157 in a food handler → needs clear stool samples before returning.
hq_q.ql: What is the minimum exclusion period before he can return to work as a food handler?

c: last episode of diarrhoea or vomiting was 24 hours ago
tm.m: Norovirus has a very low infectious dose (<20 viral particles) and continues to be shed in high titres for 48 hours after clinical symptoms resolve.
tm.g: Food handler with norovirus gastroenteritis -> return 48 hours after last vomiting/diarrhoea episode
x: A 5-day exclusion rule applies to pertussis (on antibiotics) or measles rash onset, whereas norovirus requires 48 hours symptom-free.
Returning at 24 hours carries a high risk of foodborne outbreak transmission because viral shedding remains high during the first 48 hours.
Microbiological stool clearance is mandatory for food handlers infected with Escherichia coli O157, Salmonella typhi/paratyphi or Shigella dysenteriae, not norovirus.
Disposable gloves do not prevent aerosol or fomite transmission of norovirus in a commercial kitchen.
f: a child with scarlet fever or pertussis had started appropriate antibiotics and required standard school exclusion guidance
he had experienced simple non-infective morning sickness or travel motion sickness without infectious gastroenteritis
stool culture in a commercial food handler had isolated verocytotoxin-producing Escherichia coli O157 or Salmonella typhi
he had a simple healed non-infected paper cut on his finger covered by a waterproof blue plaster and glove

hq_q.s:
A 23 year old woman presents with a 4-month history of non-bloody diarrhoea, colicky right iliac fossa pain and 5 kg unintentional weight loss. She smokes 15 cigarettes daily and has recurrent painful aphthous mouth ulcers.
Temperature 37.3°C, pulse rate 86 bpm. Examination reveals right iliac fossa tenderness and a fleshy perianal skin tag.
Ileocolonoscopy shows patchy deep serpiginous ulcers separated by normal mucosa, and biopsies show transmural inflammation with non-caseating granulomas.
hq_q.w: Crohn's disease can affect any part of the gastrointestinal tract from mouth to anus, characteristically involving the terminal ileum and perianal region. Endoscopy shows discontinuous skip lesions and cobblestone ulceration, while histology shows transmural inflammation and non-caseating granulomas. Smoking increases Crohn's risk.
hq_q.f: Caseating granulomas in a migrant from a high-incidence area → intestinal TB.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most likely diagnosis?

tm.m: Aberrant Th1/Th17 mucosal immune responses produce full-thickness (transmural) bowel wall inflammation, fissuring ulcers and non-caseating epithelioid granulomas.
tm.g: Skip lesions + perianal disease + transmural inflammation + non-caseating granulomas -> Crohn's disease
x: Ischaemic colitis affects older arteriopathic patients at the splenic flexure watershed, presenting with acute left-sided pain and bloody diarrhoea.
Microscopic colitis causes chronic watery diarrhoea in older women with macroscopically normal colonic mucosa on colonoscopy.
Intestinal tuberculosis occurs in migrants from endemic regions and produces confluent caseating (necrotising) granulomas positive for acid-fast bacilli.
Ulcerative colitis causes continuous mucosal inflammation extending proximally from the rectum with crypt abscesses, without skip lesions, perianal tags or transmural granulomas.
f: a 76 year old man with atrial fibrillation developed sudden left iliac fossa pain followed by bright red rectal bleeding and splenic flexure thumbprinting
a 64 year old woman taking lansoprazole had watery diarrhoea with a completely normal colonoscopy and a thickened subepithelial collagen band on biopsy
a migrant from an endemic country had night sweats, apical lung scarring and caseating ileocaecal granulomas positive for acid-fast bacilli
a non-smoker presented with bloody mucoid diarrhoea and continuous superficial friable inflammation extending from the rectum to the splenic flexure

hq_q.s:
A 29 year old woman admitted with an acute severe flare of ulcerative colitis has passed 12 bloody stools daily for 5 days despite 72 hours of intravenous hydrocortisone.
Temperature 38.4°C, pulse rate 120 bpm, BP 98/60 mmHg, respiratory rate 22 breaths per minute. Her abdomen is markedly distended and diffusely tender with Tympanic percussion and scanty bowel sounds.
Plain abdominal X-ray shows a dilated transverse colon measuring 7.5 cm in diameter with loss of haustral markings.
hq_q.w: Toxic megacolon is a life-threatening complication of acute severe colitis (or Clostridioides difficile infection), defined by non-obstructive colonic dilatation >6.0 cm (typically in the transverse colon) accompanied by systemic toxicity (fever, tachycardia, hypotension or leucocytosis). Urgent joint medical-surgical review for subtotal colectomy is required.
hq_q.f: Colon 4 cm with no systemic upset → severe colitis without megacolon.
hq_q.ql: Which acute complication has developed?

tm.m: Transmural extension of severe mucosal inflammation into the muscularis propria releases nitric oxide, paralysing colonic smooth muscle and causing acute dilatation.
tm.g: Transverse colon >6 cm + systemic toxicity (fever, tachycardia) in severe colitis -> toxic megacolon
x: Ogilvie syndrome (acute colonic pseudo-obstruction) occurs in elderly post-operative or critically ill patients without bloody colitis or mucosal ulceration.
Sigmoid volvulus occurs in older constipated patients and shows an inverted U-shaped 'coffee-bean' loop arising from the left iliac fossa.
Free perforation presents with generalized board-like peritonism and free subdiaphragmatic gas (Rigler sign) rather than isolated luminal dilatation.
Small bowel obstruction causes colicky central pain, bilious vomiting and central dilated loops (>3 cm) with valvulae conniventes rather than a 7.5 cm transverse colon.
f: an 80 year old man 4 days after hip replacement developed painless abdominal distension with caecal dilatation and no colitis or bloody diarrhoea
an elderly nursing home resident with chronic constipation had gross asymmetrical distension and a 'coffee-bean' sign pointing towards the right upper quadrant
erect chest and abdominal radiographs demonstrated free gas under both hemidiaphragms and double-wall sign (Rigler sign) with rigid peritonism
a patient with previous laparotomy had bilious vomiting, absolute constipation and dilated central bowel loops with valvulae conniventes crossing the full width

hq_q.s:
A 32 year old man with a 10-year history of pan-colonic ulcerative colitis attends his annual gastroenterology review. His bowel disease has been in complete clinical and endoscopic remission on oral mesalazine for 2 years, opening his bowels once daily with no blood.
Routine blood tests show bilirubin 28 µmol/L (<21), ALP 410 IU/L (30-130), GGT 320 IU/L (10-71) and ALT 62 IU/L (10-45). MRCP demonstrates multifocal beading and stricturing of the intra- and extrahepatic bile ducts.
hq_q.w: Extraintestinal manifestations of IBD that run a clinical course independent of bowel inflammation include primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC), ankylosing spondylitis/sacroiliitis and anterior uveitis (and often pyoderma gangrenosum). By contrast, erythema nodosum, episcleritis, aphthous ulcers and type 1 pauciarticular large-joint arthritis mirror bowel flares.
hq_q.f: Erythema nodosum that appears in a flare → settles as the bowel settles.
hq_q.ql: Which extraintestinal manifestation of inflammatory bowel disease has a course independent of bowel disease activity?

tm.m: Autoimmune periductal concentric ('onion-skin') fibrosis of intra- and extrahepatic bile ducts progresses autonomously even after total proctocolectomy.
tm.g: IBD extraintestinal feature progressing independently of bowel remission -> primary sclerosing cholangitis
x: Episcleritis parallels active intestinal inflammation and resolves when the underlying colitis flare is controlled.
Oral aphthous ulcers flare during active luminal relapses and settle when the bowel enters remission.
Type 1 (pauciarticular, asymmetric large-joint) enteropathic arthritis mirrors intestinal disease activity and resolves with control of the gut flare.
Erythema nodosum is a panniculitis triggered by active bowel inflammation that subsides as the colitis flare is treated.
f: the question asked which ocular complication flares in parallel with active colitis and causes painless sectoral redness blanching with phenylephrine
the question asked which oral mucosal lesion flares directly alongside active Crohn's or ulcerative colitis relapses
the question asked which self-limiting, non-erosive knee and ankle arthropathy flares in parallel with acute IBD relapses
the question asked which tender pretibial nodular skin eruption mirrors active intestinal flares and responds to treating the bowel

hq_q.s:
A 22 year old woman attends her GP surgery accompanied by her mother, who is concerned about her progressive weight loss over the past 6 months. The patient restricts her daily caloric intake, exercises for 2 hours daily and has had secondary amenorrhoea for 4 months.
Temperature 36.1°C, pulse rate 54 bpm, BP 96/60 mmHg. Her weight is 45.0 kg and her height is 1.65 m.
hq_q.w: Body mass index (BMI) is calculated as weight in kilograms divided by the square of height in metres (kg/m²). Here, 1.65 m squared is 2.7225 m², and 45.0 kg divided by 2.7225 m² equals 16.5 kg/m², which is in the moderately underweight (<18.5 kg/m²) range.
hq_q.f: She weighs 55 kg → BMI 20.2.
hq_q.ql: What is this patient's body mass index (BMI)?

tm.m: BMI normalises body mass against height squared (weight / height²); 45 / (1.65 x 1.65) = 45 / 2.7225 = 16.5 kg/m².
tm.g: Weight 45 kg divided by (1.65 m)² -> BMI 16.5 kg/m²
x: A BMI of 14.5 kg/m² at a height of 1.65 m would correspond to a body weight of 39.5 kg rather than 45.0 kg.
18.5 kg/m² is the lower threshold of the normal adult BMI range (corresponding to 50.4 kg at 1.65 m), not her calculated BMI.
A BMI of 20.5 kg/m² lies well within the healthy range and would require a weight of 55.8 kg at a height of 1.65 m.
27.3 is the erroneous figure obtained if weight is divided by height (45 / 1.65) without squaring the height in metres.
f: her weight had fallen to 39.5 kg at the same height of 1.65 m
she weighed 50.4 kg at a height of 1.65 m, placing her at the lower boundary of normal weight
she weighed 55.8 kg at a height of 1.65 m following successful nutritional rehabilitation
she weighed 74.3 kg at a height of 1.65 m, placing her in the overweight category

hq_q.s:
A 78 year old woman who lives alone is admitted to the medical ward with community-acquired pneumonia. She reports poor appetite for 2 months, has lost 11% of her body weight unintentionally over the past 4 months, and has eaten almost nothing for 6 days.
Her BMI is 19.2 kg/m². On admission nursing assessment, her Malnutrition Universal Screening Tool (MUST) score is calculated as 2.
o: Continue routine ward meals and rescreen in 1 week
Insert a central venous catheter for parenteral nutrition
Record a 3-day food chart and observe without intervention
Refer to a dietitian and implement a nutritional care plan
Repeat the MUST screening score in 1 month without action
hq_q.w: The Malnutrition Universal Screening Tool (MUST) stratifies malnutrition risk as 0 (low risk: routine care), 1 (medium risk: observe with 3-day food/fluid chart), and 2 or more (high risk: treat by referring to a dietitian or local nutritional support team, fortifying food/supplements and monitoring weekly).
hq_q.f: MUST 0 in hospital → routine care and rescreen weekly.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most appropriate nutritional management action?

tm.m: A MUST score >=2 identifies high malnutrition risk where early oral nutritional supplementation and dietetic intervention reduce inpatient complications and length of stay.
tm.g: Inpatient MUST score of 2 or more (high risk) -> refer to a dietitian and implement a nutritional care plan
x: Routine clinical care with weekly rescreening is the management for low-risk patients with a MUST score of 0.
Parenteral nutrition is reserved for patients with a non-functioning, inaccessible or perforated gastrointestinal tract; her gut works.
Observation with a 3-day dietary intake chart alone is the protocol for medium-risk patients (MUST score 1), whereas MUST >=2 requires active treatment.
Monthly rescreening without intervention is used for low-risk care-home residents (MUST 0) and is unsafe for an acutely ill inpatient with MUST 2.
f: her BMI was 23 kg/m² with no recent weight loss and normal intake, giving a low-risk MUST score of 0
she had high-output short bowel syndrome or prolonged paralytic ileus preventing enteral absorption
her BMI was 19.2 kg/m² with no acute 5-day starvation and 6% weight loss, giving a medium-risk MUST score of 1
she was a stable care-home resident with a normal BMI of 24 kg/m² and a MUST score of 0

hq_q.s:
A 48 year old man who drinks 750 mL of vodka daily presents with a 4-week history of progressive ankle swelling and exertional breathlessness. He lives alone and eats a diet consisting mainly of white bread and sweet tea.
Pulse rate 112 bpm (bounding), BP 132/58 mmHg. His extremities are warm with a raised JVP, pitting oedema to the knees, stocking sensory loss and absent ankle jerks. Echocardiography shows biventricular dilatation with a high cardiac output.
hq_q.w: Thiamine (vitamin B1) deficiency in chronic alcohol dependence and malnutrition causes beriberi. 'Wet' beriberi presents with peripheral arteriolar vasodilatation, wide pulse pressure, warm extremities, oedema and high-output biventricular heart failure; 'dry' beriberi causes symmetrical distal sensorimotor peripheral neuropathy.
hq_q.f: Dermatitis in sun-exposed areas, diarrhoea and confusion → niacin deficiency, pellagra.
hq_q.ql: Which micronutrient deficiency is the most likely cause of this presentation?

tm.m: Depletion of thiamine pyrophosphate impairs pyruvate dehydrogenase and alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase, causing adenosine-mediated systemic vasodilatation, myocardial ATP failure and axonal degeneration.
tm.g: High-output heart failure with warm extremities + peripheral neuropathy in alcohol dependence -> thiamine (vitamin B1) deficiency
x: Vitamin C deficiency (scurvy) impairs collagen hydroxylation, causing gingival bleeding, perifollicular haemorrhage and corkscrew hairs rather than high-output heart failure.
Vitamin B12 deficiency causes megaloblastic anaemia and subacute combined degeneration of the cord (dorsal column and corticospinal tract signs) rather than wet beriberi.
Folate deficiency causes megaloblastic macrocytic anaemia and glossitis without peripheral neuropathy or high-output cardiac failure.
Niacin deficiency causes pellagra, characterised by the triad of photosensitive dermatitis (Casal necklace), diarrhoea and dementia.
f: he presented with spongy bleeding gums, perifollicular petechiae, ecchymoses and coiled corkscrew body hairs
he had pernicious anaemia or ileal resection with macrocytosis (MCV 114 fL), loss of joint position sense and extensor plantars
he presented with fatigue, pallor and a macrocytic anaemia (MCV 110 fL) with normal neurological and cardiac examinations
he presented with a symmetrical scaly hyperpigmented rash around the neck (Casal necklace), watery diarrhoea and confusion

hq_q.s:
A 28 year old woman of East Asian heritage presents with a 12-month history of abdominal bloating, borborygmi, flatus and watery acidic stools. Symptoms consistently develop 1 to 2 hours after drinking milk or eating ice cream and resolve completely when she avoids dairy products. She has no weight loss or rectal bleeding.
Abdominal examination, full blood count and serum IgA tissue transglutaminase antibody with total IgA are all normal.
hq_q.w: Primary adult-type hypolactasia (lactase non-persistence) is genetically programmed after childhood in the majority of East Asian, African and Mediterranean populations. Unhydrolysed lactose exerts an osmotic load in the lumen and is fermented by colonic bacteria into hydrogen, methane and short-chain fatty acids, causing bloating, cramps and diarrhoea after dairy.
hq_q.f: Symptoms after bread with a positive tTG → coeliac disease.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most likely diagnosis?

c: 1 to 2 hours after drinking milk or eating ice cream
resolve completely when she avoids dairy
tissue transglutaminase antibody with total IgA are all normal
tm.m: Brush-border lactase decline leaves unabsorbed disaccharide lactose in the gut lumen, drawing water osmotically and undergoing colonic bacterial fermentation.
tm.g: Post-dairy bloating, flatulence and watery diarrhoea resolving on dairy exclusion with negative tTG -> lactose intolerance
x: Giardiasis causes persistent steatorrhoea and weight loss regardless of dairy intake following contaminated water exposure.
Coeliac disease is triggered by wheat, barley and rye gluten rather than lactose and is excluded here by negative IgA tTG with normal total IgA.
IBS causes chronic abdominal pain related to defaecation across varied foods rather than isolated, reproducible post-dairy osmotic diarrhoea.
Small intestinal bacterial overgrowth occurs in patients with structural stasis or dysmotility (such as systemic sclerosis or blind loops) causing steatorrhoea and low B12.
f: she developed persistent greasy, foul-smelling stools and weight loss after drinking untreated water on a camping trip
symptoms were triggered by bread and pasta and accompanied by iron deficiency anaemia and a positive IgA tissue transglutaminase antibody
she had crampy pain relieved by defaecation and loose stools unrelated to dairy intake with normal hydrogen breath testing
she had systemic sclerosis with persistent steatorrhoea, weight loss, elevated serum folate and low serum vitamin B12

hq_q.s:
A 42 year old man who underwent a 60 cm terminal ileal resection for stricturing Crohn's disease 3 years ago presents with progressive fatigue, symmetrical tingling in both feet and unsteadiness when walking in the dark. He eats a balanced omnivorous diet.
Neurological examination reveals impaired vibration and joint position sense in both great toes, absent ankle jerks and a positive Romberg sign.
hq_q.w: Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) bound to intrinsic factor is absorbed exclusively via cubilin receptors in the terminal ileum. After terminal ileal resection, hepatic B12 stores deplete over 2 to 4 years, causing megaloblastic macrocytic anaemia (MCV 112 fL) and subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord (dorsal column and peripheral neuropathy).
hq_q.f: Duodenal disease or resection → iron deficiency.
hq_q.ql: Which micronutrient deficiency is most likely responsible?

c: unsteadiness when walking in the dark
tm.m: Loss of terminal ileal cubilin receptors prevents intrinsic factor-B12 absorption, impairing methionine synthase and methylmalonyl-CoA mutase required for myelin maintenance and DNA synthesis.
tm.g: Terminal ileal resection + macrocytic anaemia (MCV 112 fL) + dorsal column sensory ataxia -> vitamin B12 (cobalamin) deficiency
x: Folate is absorbed in the proximal jejunum (duodenum/jejunum) rather than the terminal ileum and does not cause subacute combined degeneration of the cord.
Pyridoxine deficiency (typically from isoniazid therapy) causes isolated peripheral neuropathy and sideroblastic microcytic anaemia rather than MCV 112 fL after ileal resection.
Thiamine deficiency occurs in alcohol dependence or hyperemesis, causing Wernicke encephalopathy or beriberi with a normal MCV rather than post-ileectomy macrocytosis.
Vitamin D deficiency causes osteomalacia with bone pain and proximal myopathy rather than megaloblastic anaemia and dorsal column sensory ataxia.
f: a patient on methotrexate or phenytoin developed macrocytic anaemia (MCV 110 fL) with a completely normal neurological examination
a patient taking isoniazid for tuberculosis without vitamin supplementation developed stocking numbness and a microcytic sideroblastic blood film
a heavy drinker presented with acute confusion, sixth nerve palsy and broad-based cerebellar ataxia with normal MCV
a housebound patient presented with diffuse bone pain, waddling proximal myopathy, hypocalcaemia and raised alkaline phosphatase

hq_q.s:
A 70 year old woman with limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis presents with a 4-month history of postprandial bloating, flatulence, loose pale stools and 4 kg weight loss.
Temperature 36.6°C, pulse rate 74 bpm. Examination shows sclerodactyly, perioral skin tethering and mild non-tender abdominal distension.
Blood tests show elevated serum folate, low serum vitamin B12 and negative IgA tissue transglutaminase antibodies.
hq_q.w: Systemic sclerosis causes smooth muscle atrophy and fibrosis of the small intestine, impairing the migrating motor complex and promoting small bowel bacterial overgrowth (SIBO). Overgrown luminal bacteria deconjugate bile salts (causing steatorrhoea), competitively consume vitamin B12, and synthesise folate (raising serum folate). Confirm with a glucose/lactulose hydrogen breath test and treat with rifaximin.
hq_q.f: Watery diarrhoea after cholecystectomy → bile acid diarrhoea.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most likely diagnosis?

tm.m: Small-intestinal hypomotility allows colonic-type flora to proliferate proximally; bacteria consume cobalamin (lowering B12), synthesise folic acid (raising folate) and deconjugate bile acids.
tm.g: Gut dysmotility (systemic sclerosis) + steatorrhoea + high serum folate + low serum B12 -> small bowel bacterial overgrowth
x: Coeliac disease causes proximal small-bowel villous atrophy resulting in low serum folate and iron deficiency with positive tTG serology, rather than high serum folate.
Bile acid malabsorption follows terminal ileal disease or cholecystectomy and causes watery secretory diarrhoea rather than elevated serum folate in systemic sclerosis.
Secondary lactose intolerance causes transient dairy-triggered watery diarrhoea after acute gastroenteritis without altering vitamin B12 or raising serum folate.
Whipple's disease is a rare Tropheryma whipplei infection in middle-aged men causing arthralgia, hyperpigmentation, dementia and PAS-positive macrophages.
f: blood tests showed low serum folate, low ferritin and strongly positive IgA tissue transglutaminase antibodies
she developed chronic watery diarrhoea after a terminal ileal resection or cholecystectomy with a 7-day SeHCAT retention of 4%
a patient developed transient bloating and loose stools exclusively after drinking milk for 3 weeks following acute rotavirus gastroenteritis
a 52 year old man presented with migratory arthralgia, skin hyperpigmentation, cognitive decline and PAS-positive macrophages on duodenal biopsy

hq_q.s:
A 34 year old woman presents with an 8-month history of fatigue, postprandial bloating and loose, bulky stools. She eats a regular diet containing wheat bread and pasta. Blood tests show haemoglobin 102 g/L (115-150), MCV 73 fL (80-96) and ferritin 6 µg/L (12-200).
Upper GI endoscopy and distal duodenal biopsies demonstrate subtotal villous atrophy, crypt hyperplasia and markedly increased intraepithelial lymphocytes.
hq_q.w: Coeliac disease is an autoimmune enteropathy triggered by dietary gluten gliadin peptides in HLA-DQ2/DQ8 positive individuals. Proximal small-bowel involvement impairs iron and folate absorption, and duodenal biopsies taken while eating gluten show the classic Marsh triad: intraepithelial lymphocytosis, crypt hyperplasia and villous atrophy.
hq_q.f: PAS-positive macrophages in the lamina propria → Whipple's disease.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most likely diagnosis?

c: subtotal villous atrophy, crypt hyperplasia and markedly increased intraepithelial lymphocytes
tm.m: Tissue transglutaminase deamidates gliadin peptides, which bind HLA-DQ2/DQ8 on antigen-presenting cells and activate CD4+ T cells to destroy duodenal villi.
tm.g: Iron deficiency anaemia + duodenal villous atrophy, crypt hyperplasia and raised intraepithelial lymphocytes on gluten -> coeliac disease
x: Giardiasis follows contaminated water exposure and shows pear-shaped trophozoites on the mucosal surface without classic autoimmune Marsh triad and iron deficiency.
Crohn's disease causes patchy aphthous/deep fissuring ulceration, transmural inflammation and non-caseating granulomas rather than diffuse villous atrophy.
Tropical sprue occurs in residents or long-term travellers to tropical regions and typically presents with megaloblastic folate/B12 deficiency.
Whipple's disease shows lamina propria infiltration by foamy macrophages staining strongly positive with periodic acid-Schiff (PAS).
f: she developed acute-on-chronic greasy diarrhoea after drinking untreated mountain stream water and biopsy showed surface flagellated trophozoites
endoscopy showed patchy cobblestoning, perianal fistulae and transmural inflammation with non-caseating granulomas
she had lived in rural South India for 2 years and presented with chronic diarrhoea, glossitis and severe folate deficiency responsive to tetracycline
duodenal biopsy demonstrated distended villi packed with foamy PAS-positive macrophages in a patient with migratory arthralgia

hq_q.s:
A 28 year old woman is newly diagnosed with biopsy-proven coeliac disease after presenting with iron deficiency anaemia and steatorrhoea. She has commenced a strict gluten-free diet under dietetic supervision.
Pulse rate 74 bpm, BP 116/72 mmHg. A peripheral blood film performed during her work-up demonstrates target cells, acanthocytes and nuclear remnant Howell-Jolly bodies within erythrocytes.
hq_q.w: Coeliac disease is associated with functional hyposplenism in up to 30% of adult patients, evidenced on the blood film by Howell-Jolly bodies (nuclear DNA remnants normally pitted by a healthy spleen). Hyposplenism predisposes to overwhelming sepsis from encapsulated bacteria, mandating pneumococcal (plus MenACWY, MenB and annual influenza) vaccination.
hq_q.f: Howell-Jolly bodies on the blood film → confirms hyposplenism.
hq_q.ql: Which vaccination is specifically recommended in light of her blood film finding?

tm.m: Splenic atrophy in coeliac disease impairs reticuloendothelial clearance of opsonised encapsulated bacteria (Streptococcus pneumoniae, Neisseria meningitidis, Haemophilus influenzae) and nuclear remnants.
tm.g: Coeliac disease with Howell-Jolly bodies (functional hyposplenism) -> pneumococcal vaccine
x: BCG is a live attenuated vaccine against Mycobacterium tuberculosis and has no role in protecting hyposplenic patients against encapsulated bacteria.
HPV vaccination is part of the routine adolescent schedule to prevent cervical and anogenital neoplasia, not an immunisation for hyposplenism.
Hepatitis A vaccine is indicated for travel to endemic areas or chronic liver disease, not functional hyposplenism.
Typhoid vaccination is a travel vaccine for endemic regions and is not part of the UK hyposplenism immunisation schedule.
f: an Mantoux-negative healthcare worker was starting employment in a high-risk multidrug-resistant tuberculosis unit
a 13 year old school pupil was attending for routine adolescent vaccination against cervical and head-and-neck cancer
a patient with chronic hepatitis C cirrhosis or travelling to a developing country required protection against enterically transmitted viral hepatitis
she was travelling to rural South Asia for 6 weeks to visit friends and relatives

hq_q.s:
A 61 year old man with a 20-year history of coeliac disease presents with a 3-month history of colicky central abdominal pain, drenching night sweats, anorexia and 8 kg unintentional weight loss. A specialist dietitian confirms strict adherence to his gluten-free diet, and serum IgA tissue transglutaminase antibody is negative.
Temperature 37.8°C. Abdominal examination reveals a deep, ill-defined central abdominal mass.
hq_q.w: Long-standing coeliac disease carries a significantly increased risk of enteropathy-associated T-cell lymphoma (EATL) and small-bowel adenocarcinoma. Recurrence of abdominal pain, weight loss, B symptoms (night sweats, fever) or an abdominal mass despite strict gluten exclusion (negative tTG) mandates urgent CT/MR enterography and enteroscopy.
hq_q.f: Symptoms come back after eating out → hidden gluten.
hq_q.ql: Which complication of coeliac disease is most important to exclude?
hq_q.post: Tissue transglutaminase antibody is negative.

tm.m: Chronic mucosal intraepithelial T-cell stimulation can evolve through refractory coeliac disease type II into clonal malignant CD3+/CD8- enteropathy-associated T-cell lymphoma.
tm.g: B symptoms (night sweats, weight loss), pain and abdominal mass despite strict gluten-free diet -> enteropathy-associated T-cell lymphoma
x: Dermatitis herpetiformis is an intensely itchy symmetrical vesicular rash on the elbows, knees and buttocks caused by epidermal IgA deposits, not an abdominal mass with night sweats.
Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency can cause persistent steatorrhoea in coeliac disease but does not cause drenching night sweats, fever or a palpable abdominal mass.
Microscopic colitis causes non-bloody watery diarrhoea and is more common in coeliac disease, but never produces night sweats, severe weight loss or a central mass.
Lactose intolerance causes post-dairy bloating and loose stools without systemic B symptoms, anaemia, hypoalbuminaemia or an abdominal mass.
f: he developed intensely pruritic clustered vesicles and excoriated papules over the extensor surfaces of both elbows and knees
he had persistent painless floating steatorrhoea despite a gluten-free diet with no B symptoms and a faecal elastase of 45 µg/g
he had persistent watery non-bloody diarrhoea with no weight loss or night sweats and increased intraepithelial lymphocytes on colonic biopsy
he had isolated postprandial bloating and loose stools 1 hour after drinking cow's milk with normal weight and albumin

hq_q.s:
A 55 year old postmenopausal woman presents to her GP with a 2-month history of daily abdominal bloating, early satiety after small meals and mild lower pelvic discomfort. She reports increased urinary urgency, while her bowel habit remains unchanged and she has no previous gastrointestinal history.
Temperature 36.6°C, pulse rate 74 bpm. Abdominal examination reveals mild distension with no palpable organomegaly. Full blood count is normal.
o: Serum IgA tTG and IgA1 serology
hq_q.w: Under NICE suspected cancer guidelines (NG12), any woman (especially aged 50 or over) presenting with persistent or frequent (>12 times per month) abdominal distension/bloating, early satiety, pelvic pain or urinary urgency including new 'IBS-like' symptoms must have serum CA-125 measured first; if >=35 IU/mL, arrange an urgent pelvic ultrasound.
hq_q.f: A 26-year-old with years of symptoms relieved by opening her bowels → IBS.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most appropriate initial investigation in primary care?

tm.m: Epithelial ovarian carcinoma spreads transcoelomically across the peritoneum and omentum, presenting insidiously with subacute bloating, early satiety and pelvic pressure.
tm.g: New persistent bloating and early satiety in a woman aged 50 or over -> serum CA-125 measurement first
x: Stool culture investigates acute infective diarrhoea; she has normal bowel habit with persistent bloating and early satiety.
Coeliac serology is appropriate for investigating chronic diarrhoea or iron deficiency in younger adults, whereas in a 55 year old woman ovarian cancer must be excluded first.
Faecal calprotectin differentiates IBD from IBS in adults under 40 with diarrhoea, while FIT investigates colorectal change in bowel habit or iron deficiency.
Colonoscopy investigates lower GI bleeding, positive FIT or altered bowel habit; her bowel habit is normal and ovarian malignancy is the key mimic to exclude.
f: she presented with acute febrile watery diarrhoea lasting 8 days after returning from travel abroad
a 28 year old woman presented with chronic loose stools, postprandial bloating and microcytic iron deficiency anaemia
she presented with a 6-week change in bowel habit to looser stools with iron deficiency anaemia requiring quantitative faecal haemoglobin testing
she had a positive quantitative faecal immunochemical test (FIT >10 µg Hb/g) and unexplained iron deficiency anaemia

hq_q.s:
A 30 year old man presents to his GP with a 2-year history of recurrent crampy lower abdominal pain relieved by defaecation, associated with passing 4 to 5 loose watery stools daily and urgency. He has no rectal bleeding, nocturnal symptoms or weight loss.
Abdominal examination, full blood count, CRP, IgA tissue transglutaminase and faecal calprotectin are all normal, confirming diarrhoea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome.
hq_q.w: Under NICE guidelines (CG61), oral loperamide is the first-line antimotility agent for diarrhoea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D), titrated carefully according to stool consistency and taken prophylactically before situations where urgency is problematic.
hq_q.f: Constipation-predominant IBS → ispaghula husk.
hq_q.ql: Which is the first-line pharmacological treatment to control his bowel frequency?

tm.m: Loperamide is a peripheral mu-opioid receptor agonist in the myenteric plexus that does not cross the blood-brain barrier, slowing colonic transit and increasing anal sphincter tone.
tm.g: First-line antimotility drug for diarrhoea-predominant IBS -> oral loperamide
x: Codeine crosses the blood-brain barrier, causing sedation, tolerance and opioid dependence, so it is not recommended for chronic IBS-D.
Lactulose is a synthetic disaccharide osmotic laxative that worsens diarrhoea and is explicitly discouraged in IBS by NICE because colonic fermentation worsens bloating.
Linaclotide is a guanylate cyclase-C agonist that stimulates intestinal fluid secretion and is licensed for refractory constipation-predominant IBS (IBS-C), not IBS-D.
Metronidazole is an antiprotozoal and anaerobic antibiotic used for Giardia or Clostridioides difficile and has no role in non-infective IBS-D.
f: short-term step-2 opioid analgesia was required for acute post-operative somatic pain in a non-IBS patient
a patient with decompensated hepatic cirrhosis required bowel acidification and catharsis to treat hepatic encephalopathy
he had severe constipation-predominant IBS lasting over 12 months that had failed optimal trials of macrogol and stimulant laxatives
stool microscopy or antigen testing had confirmed Giardia lamblia trophozoites after drinking untreated stream water

hq_q.s:
A 32 year old woman with confirmed irritable bowel syndrome attends her GP for review. For the past 3 months she has adhered to first-line lifestyle and dietary measures (eating regular meals, drinking 8 cups of fluid daily, reducing caffeine, alcohol and carbonated drinks, and limiting insoluble wheat bran), but daily abdominal bloating and flatulence still disrupt her work.
Coeliac serology and faecal calprotectin are normal.
o: Two-week course of oral rifaximin antibiotics
hq_q.w: When bloating, pain and bowel symptoms in irritable bowel syndrome persist despite first-line dietary and lifestyle advice, NICE recommends referral to a trained healthcare professional/dietitian for a structured trial of a low-FODMAP diet (restricting fermentable oligosaccharides, disaccharides, monosaccharides and polyols for 4-8 weeks, followed by stepwise reintroduction).
hq_q.f: She wants to try a probiotic → use one for at least 4 weeks.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most appropriate next dietary intervention?

c: adhered to first-line lifestyle and dietary measures
bloating and flatulence still disrupt her work
tm.m: Short-chain fermentable carbohydrates (FODMAPs) are poorly absorbed in the small bowel, drawing water osmotically and undergoing rapid colonic bacterial fermentation into hydrogen and methane gas.
tm.g: Persistent IBS bloating despite first-line diet advice -> dietitian-led low-FODMAP exclusion diet
x: NICE specifically advises against insoluble fibre such as wheat bran in IBS because it exacerbates bloating, wind and abdominal cramps.
Coeliac disease has been excluded, so a lifelong strict gluten-free diet is unnecessary; wheat fructans (a FODMAP) rather than gluten protein usually drive IBS bloating.
NICE states that if a patient chooses to trial a probiotic in IBS, it must be taken for at least 4 weeks at the manufacturer's dose to assess efficacy.
Rifaximin is used for hepatic encephalopathy or confirmed small intestinal bacterial overgrowth, not routine primary-care IBS management in the UK.
f: soluble fibre such as ispaghula husk or oats (rather than insoluble wheat bran) was being recommended for constipation-predominant IBS
her IgA tissue transglutaminase serology and duodenal biopsy had confirmed coeliac disease
a patient opted for a trial of probiotics for at least 4 weeks while monitoring symptom response
a lactulose/glucose hydrogen breath test in a patient with systemic sclerosis confirmed small intestinal bacterial overgrowth

hq_q.s:
A 60 year old woman presents with a 12-month history of retrosternal heartburn, effortless postprandial regurgitation and intermittent postprandial chest fullness, worse on bending forward or lying flat. Her BMI is 33 kg/m².
Upper GI endoscopy demonstrates Los Angeles grade B reflux oesophagitis and a large hiatus hernia. The upper GI surgical team wishes to delineate the exact size, type and anatomical position of the hernia prior to anti-reflux surgery.
o: High-resolution CT scan of the thorax
hq_q.w: A barium swallow (upper GI contrast fluoroscopy) is the most sensitive test for delineating the size, anatomical type (sliding Type I vs paraoesophageal rolling Type II-IV) and relation of the gastro-oesophageal junction and gastric fundus to the diaphragmatic hiatus prior to surgical repair.
hq_q.f: Dysphagia or weight loss → upper GI endoscopy first.
hq_q.ql: Which investigation best demonstrates the anatomical configuration of a hiatus hernia?

c: delineate the exact size, type and anatomical position
tm.m: Dynamic real-time barium fluoroscopy outlines the gastro-oesophageal junction, gastric cardia/fundus and diaphragmatic crura throughout swallowing and posture changes.
tm.g: Best investigation to define hiatus hernia anatomy before surgery -> barium swallow contrast study
x: Ambulatory 24-hour pH-impedance monitoring quantifies acid exposure time and symptom correlation, but provides zero anatomical imaging of the hernia.
High-resolution lung-window CT assesses pulmonary parenchyma rather than providing dynamic mucosal and junctional contrast views of a hiatus hernia.
A plain chest X-ray may incidentally show a retrocardiac air-fluid level in a large hernia but cannot define junctional anatomy for surgical planning.
Ultrasound is obscured by intraluminal gastric gas and the thoracic ribcage and cannot image an intrathoracic hiatus hernia.
f: endoscopy was completely normal and objective quantification of acid reflux episodes was required before fundoplication
she presented with bibasal velcro crackles and finger clubbing requiring parenchymal evaluation for interstitial lung disease
