hq_q.s: A 35 year old woman gave birth 3 days ago following labour analgesia with a lumbar epidural. Since yesterday she has experienced a severe fronto-occipital headache that develops within 5 minutes of sitting or standing and resolves completely within 15 minutes of lying flat. Temperature is 36.8°C, pulse rate 76 bpm and BP 118/72 mmHg. Neurological examination and fundoscopy are normal, with no photophobia.
hq_q.w: Post-dural puncture headache results from cerebrospinal fluid leakage through a dural tear, causing intracranial hypotension and traction on pain-sensitive meninges when upright. Conservative management includes hydration, analgesia and caffeine, with epidural blood patch if persistent.
hq_q.f: Postpartum headache worse lying flat with seizures and papilloedema -> cerebral venous sinus thrombosis.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most likely diagnosis?

c: within 5 minutes of sitting or standing
resolves completely within 15 minutes of lying flat
tm.m: Cerebrospinal fluid leakage lowers intracranial pressure, causing downward traction on pain-sensitive meninges when upright.
tm.g: Strict orthostatic headache within days of neuraxial anaesthesia -> Post-dural puncture headache
f: postpartum headache worse on lying down accompanied by focal seizures and papilloedema
headache worse on lying flat with bilateral optic disc swelling and elevated CSF opening pressure
pulsatile unilateral headache with nausea and photophobia unaffected by posture
sudden-onset occipital thunderclap headache with photophobia, vomiting and meningism
x: Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis causes a progressive headache worse on lying flat or Valsalva, often with seizures or focal neurology.
Idiopathic intracranial hypertension causes headache worse on waking and bending forward, accompanied by papilloedema and visual obscurations.
Migraine causes throbbing unilateral headache with nausea and photophobia rather than strict orthostatic relief on lying flat.
Subarachnoid haemorrhage presents with a sudden thunderclap headache reaching maximal intensity within seconds, not a purely postural headache after epidural.

hq_q.s:
A 42 year old woman has had a headache for 3 weeks that comes on within minutes of standing and is relieved by lying flat. She has had no lumbar puncture or epidural. Neurological examination is normal.
MRI brain with contrast shows smooth thickening and enhancement of the meninges, sagging of the brain and small subdural fluid collections.
hq_q.w: Low CSF volume makes the brain sag and the meninges swell. Small subdural collections can form.
hq_q.f: Meningeal enhancement with fever and a stiff neck → meningitis.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most likely diagnosis?

tm.m: A spontaneous CSF leak lowers pressure so the brain sags and the meninges swell
tm.g: Postural headache with meningeal enhancement and brain sag is spontaneous intracranial hypotension
f: meningeal enhancement with fever and a stiff neck
the presentation instead showed features specific to Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (Venous sinus thrombosis causes raised pressure, not a postural headache)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Leptomeningeal metastases (Leptomeningeal metastases cause nodular enhancement and are not postural)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Subarachnoid haemorrhage (SAH is sudden and severe, not a postural headache over 3 weeks)
x: Ruled out here: requires meningeal enhancement with fever and a stiff neck, whereas this patient has relieved by lying flat, no lumbar puncture or epidural.
Venous sinus thrombosis causes raised pressure, not a postural headache.
Leptomeningeal metastases cause nodular enhancement and are not postural.
SAH is sudden and severe, not a postural headache over 3 weeks.

hq_q.s: A 28 year old woman has had a post-dural puncture headache for 3 days after a spinal anaesthetic. Bed rest, oral fluids, regular analgesia and caffeine have not helped. She cannot care for her baby.
hq_q.w: An epidural blood patch seals the leak and usually works quickly. Key discriminator: Disabling PDPH after conservative care: epidural blood patch.
hq_q.f: Symptoms are mild and improving on day 1 → conservative care.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most appropriate treatment?

tm.m: Injected blood seals the dural hole
tm.g: Disabling PDPH after conservative care: epidural blood patch
f: the presentation instead showed features specific to Lumbar drain (Removing more CSF worsens intracranial hypotension and post-dural puncture headache)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Morphine (Opioids do not seal the leak; a blood patch does)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Repeat lumbar puncture (Creating a second dural puncture worsens CSF leakage and headache)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Triptan (Triptans are for migraine, not a CSF leak)
x: Removing more CSF worsens intracranial hypotension and post-dural puncture headache
Opioids do not seal the leak; a blood patch does.
Creating a second dural puncture worsens CSF leakage and headache
Triptans are for migraine, not a CSF leak.

hq_q.s: A 52 year old woman with JAK2-positive polycythaemia vera presents with a 2-week history of progressive right upper quadrant pain and rapid abdominal distension. Temperature is 36.9°C, pulse rate 92 bpm and BP 126/78 mmHg. She is anicteric and her jugular venous pressure is not elevated. Abdominal examination reveals a markedly tender liver edge 6 cm below the costal margin and shifting dullness.
hq_q.w: Budd-Chiari syndrome is hepatic venous outflow obstruction, presenting with the classic triad of abdominal pain, tender hepatomegaly and ascites with a normal jugular venous pressure. Myeloproliferative neoplasms such as polycythaemia vera are the commonest underlying prothrombotic cause.
hq_q.f: Painful hepatomegaly and ascites with an elevated JVP and ankle oedema -> right heart failure or constrictive pericarditis.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most likely diagnosis?

c: jugular venous pressure is not elevated
tender liver edge 6 cm below the costal margin and shifting dullness
tm.m: Hepatic vein thrombosis obstructs venous outflow, causing acute sinusoidal congestion, painful hepatomegaly and portal hypertension.
tm.g: Triad of abdominal pain, tender hepatomegaly and ascites in a prothrombotic state with normal JVP -> Budd-Chiari syndrome
f: jaundice, fever and tender hepatomegaly with an AST:ALT ratio above 2 in a heavy drinker
ascites and hepatomegaly with a markedly raised JVP, pericardial knock and Kussmaul's sign
acute abdominal pain with splenomegaly and variceal bleeding but a normal-sized non-tender liver
hepatomegaly and ascites accompanied by a raised JVP, right ventricular heave and bilateral leg oedema
x: Alcoholic hepatitis presents with fever, deep jaundice and a history of heavy alcohol excess rather than sudden ascites in polycythaemia vera.
Constrictive pericarditis causes hepatic congestion and ascites but always elevates the jugular venous pressure with Kussmaul's sign.
Portal vein thrombosis causes splenomegaly and variceal bleeding without painful hepatic venous congestion or tender hepatomegaly.
Right heart failure causes congestive hepatomegaly and ascites only alongside an elevated jugular venous pressure and pitting ankle oedema.

hq_q.s:
A 34 year old woman taking the combined oral contraceptive pill has had right upper quadrant pain and abdominal swelling for 10 days.
There is tender hepatomegaly and ascites. The JVP is normal. Budd-Chiari syndrome is suspected.
hq_q.w: Doppler ultrasound shows absent or reversed flow in the hepatic veins. CT or MR venography confirm.
hq_q.f: Ultrasound shows a clot in the portal vein instead → portal vein thrombosis.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most appropriate first investigation?

tm.m: Doppler shows absent or reversed hepatic vein flow
tm.g: Suspected Budd-Chiari: Doppler ultrasound of the liver
f: the presentation instead showed features specific to Diagnostic ascitic tap for protein (Ascitic protein does not confirm a hepatic vein clot)
the presentation instead showed features specific to ERCP (ERCP looks at bile ducts, not the hepatic veins)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Percutaneous liver biopsy (Biopsy is invasive and does not show the veins)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Upper GI endoscopy (Endoscopy looks for varices, not the cause of hepatomegaly with ascites)
x: Ascitic protein does not confirm a hepatic vein clot.
ERCP looks at bile ducts, not the hepatic veins.
Biopsy is invasive and does not show the veins.
Endoscopy looks for varices, not the cause of hepatomegaly with ascites.

hq_q.s: A 48 year old woman has Budd-Chiari syndrome confirmed on Doppler ultrasound and CT venography, with thrombosis of the hepatic veins. She has a JAK2 mutation. Her liver function is mildly impaired and there is no variceal bleeding.
hq_q.w: Anticoagulate all patients, treat the cause, then angioplasty, TIPS or transplant in a stepwise way.
hq_q.f: Not improving on anticoagulation → angioplasty or TIPS.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most appropriate first treatment?

tm.m: Anticoagulation stops the clot extending and lets the veins recanalise
tm.g: Budd-Chiari: anticoagulation first
f: the presentation instead showed features specific to Aspirin (Aspirin does not treat venous thrombosis; anticoagulation is needed)
liver failure despite all treatment
the presentation instead showed features specific to Steroids (Steroids do not treat a venous clot)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Watch and wait (Untreated hepatic vein thrombosis progresses to fulminant liver failure or cirrhosis)
x: Aspirin does not treat venous thrombosis; anticoagulation is needed.
Ruled out here: requires liver failure despite all treatment, whereas this patient has JAK2 mutation, no variceal bleeding.
Steroids do not treat a venous clot.
Untreated hepatic vein thrombosis progresses to fulminant liver failure or cirrhosis

hq_q.s: A 72 year old man with Lewy body dementia has become distressed. His daughter says he is convinced that his wife has been replaced by an identical impostor. He is otherwise orientated.
hq_q.w: Capgras: a familiar person replaced by a double. Seen in schizophrenia, dementia and after brain injury.
hq_q.f: Believes different strangers are one person in disguise → Fregoli syndrome.
hq_q.ql: Which term best describes this?

tm.m: Recognition without the feeling of familiarity leads to a belief in a double
tm.g: Belief that a familiar person is replaced by a double is Capgras syndrome
f: believes he is dead or rotting
believes a famous person loves him
the presentation instead showed features specific to Ekbom syndrome (Ekbom syndrome is the belief of being infested with insects)
believes different strangers are one person in disguise
x: Ruled out here: requires believes he is dead or rotting, whereas this patient has replaced by an identical impostor, A 72 year old man with.
Ruled out here: requires believes a famous person loves him, whereas this patient has replaced by an identical impostor, A 72 year old man with.
Ekbom syndrome is the belief of being infested with insects.
Ruled out here: requires believes different strangers are one person in disguise, whereas this patient has replaced by an identical impostor, A 72 year old man with.

hq_q.s:
A 58 year old woman is convinced that insects are living under her skin. She brings small bits of fluff and skin in a matchbox as proof. Several dermatology examinations and skin scrapings have been normal.
There are excoriations on her arms but no burrows or other skin disease.
hq_q.w: Delusional parasitosis, Ekbom syndrome, is a fixed false belief of infestation. People often bring samples in boxes.
hq_q.f: Fixed belief that a partner is unfaithful → Othello syndrome, morbid jealousy.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most likely diagnosis?

c: insects are living under her skin
tm.m: A fixed false belief of infestation persists despite normal tests
tm.g: Fixed belief of skin infestation with normal tests is delusional parasitosis
f: believes a relative has been replaced by an impostor
the presentation instead showed features specific to Hypochondriasis (Hypochondriasis is fear of illness, not a fixed belief of infestation)
a fixed belief that a partner is unfaithful
many physical symptoms across systems over years
x: Ruled out here: requires believes a relative has been replaced by an impostor, whereas this patient has insects are living under her skin, matchbox.
Hypochondriasis is fear of illness, not a fixed belief of infestation.
Ruled out here: requires a fixed belief that a partner is unfaithful, whereas this patient has insects are living under her skin, matchbox.
Ruled out here: requires many physical symptoms across systems over years, whereas this patient has insects are living under her skin, matchbox.

hq_q.s: A 46 year old man has a fixed belief that his wife is having an affair, despite no evidence. He checks her phone several times a day, follows her to work and accuses her repeatedly. He drinks heavily at weekends.
hq_q.w: Morbid jealousy carries a real risk of violence and homicide. Ask about threats and safety, and consider safeguarding.
hq_q.f: Belief that a celebrity loves him → de Clérambault syndrome, with risk of stalking.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most important risk to assess?

c: fixed belief that his wife is having an affair
tm.m: Morbid jealousy, worse with alcohol, carries a real risk of violence and homicide
tm.g: Morbid jealousy: assess the risk of violence towards his partner
f: the presentation instead showed features specific to Alcohol misuse (Alcohol is a factor, but violence to his partner is the most important risk)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Self-neglect at home (Self-neglect is not the main concern in morbid jealousy)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Stalking a famous person (Stalking a famous person is erotomania)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Suicide by overdose (Suicide is a risk, but the partner is in most danger)
x: Alcohol is a factor, but violence to his partner is the most important risk.
Self-neglect is not the main concern in morbid jealousy.
Stalking a famous person is erotomania.
Suicide is a risk, but the partner is in most danger.

hq_q.s:
A 30 year old man still lives with his mother. He cannot make everyday decisions, such as what to wear, without her reassurance. He avoids disagreeing with anyone in case they stop supporting him and feels helpless and anxious when alone.
He has no low mood, panic attacks or psychotic symptoms.
hq_q.w: Dependent: excessive need to be cared for, clinging, and fear of being alone or making decisions.
hq_q.f: Wants friendships but avoids them for fear of rejection and criticism → anxious avoidant.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most likely diagnosis?

tm.m: A pervasive need to be cared for drives clinging and fear of separation
tm.g: Needing reassurance for every decision with fear of being alone is dependent personality
f: wants friends but avoids them for fear of criticism
the presentation instead showed features specific to Generalised anxiety disorder (GAD is worry about many things, not needing others to make every decision)
perfectionism and rigidity with lists and rules
the presentation instead showed features specific to Social anxiety disorder (Social anxiety is fear of being judged by others, not needing others to make decisions)
x: Ruled out here: requires wants friends but avoids them for fear of criticism, whereas this patient has cannot make everyday decisions, avoids disagreeing.
GAD is worry about many things, not needing others to make every decision.
Ruled out here: requires perfectionism and rigidity with lists and rules, whereas this patient has cannot make everyday decisions, avoids disagreeing.
Social anxiety is fear of being judged by others, not needing others to make decisions.

hq_q.s: A 44 year old woman is a perfectionist who cannot delegate at work because she believes no one else will do the job properly. She is rigid about rules, lists and schedules, and her work comes before friends and family. She sees nothing wrong with how she behaves and has no intrusive thoughts.
hq_q.w: Anankastic personality traits are ego-syntonic: she believes her way is right. OCD thoughts are unwanted and resisted.
hq_q.f: Unwanted intrusive thoughts she resists with rituals → OCD.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most likely diagnosis?

c: rigid about rules, lists and schedules
tm.m: Anankastic traits are ego-syntonic; OCD thoughts are unwanted
tm.g: Ego-syntonic perfectionism and rigidity without intrusive thoughts is anankastic personality
f: the presentation instead showed features specific to Autism spectrum disorder (Autism starts in early childhood with social communication difficulty, not perfectionism at work)
cannot make everyday decisions + avoids disagreeing
the presentation instead showed features specific to Generalised anxiety disorder (GAD is distressing worry; her rigidity feels right to her)
unwanted intrusive thoughts resisted with rituals
x: Autism starts in early childhood with social communication difficulty, not perfectionism at work.
Ruled out here: requires cannot make everyday decisions + avoids disagreeing, whereas this patient has cannot delegate, rigid about rules, lists and schedules.
GAD is distressing worry; her rigidity feels right to her.
Ruled out here: requires unwanted intrusive thoughts resisted with rituals, whereas this patient has cannot delegate, rigid about rules, lists and schedules.

hq_q.s: A 26 year old man has felt inferior and socially inept since his early teens. He would like friends and a partner but avoids social events, and he turned down a promotion because he was sure he would be criticised. He joins in when he is certain people like him. He has no low mood or panic attacks.
hq_q.w: Avoidant (anxious) personality disorder is a pervasive pattern from adolescence of feeling inferior and unappealing, fearing criticism and rejection, and avoiding social and work contact despite wanting it. It sits in cluster C with dependent and anankastic personality disorders.
hq_q.f: Prefers to be alone, has no wish for close relationships and is indifferent to praise or criticism → schizoid personality disorder.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most likely diagnosis?

tm.m: A lifelong fear of rejection drives avoidance of the contact he wants
tm.g: Wants contact but avoids it for fear of criticism, since adolescence: avoidant
f: the presentation instead showed features specific to Autism spectrum disorder (Autism shows from early childhood with social communication differences and restricted interests, not fear of criticism in someone who wants friends)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Dependent personality disorder (Dependent personality disorder centres on needing others to make decisions and fear of being left alone)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Schizoid personality disorder (Schizoid personality disorder is detachment with no wish for relationships; he wants friends but is afraid)

the presentation instead showed features specific to Social anxiety disorder (Social anxiety disorder is fear of particular social or performance situations; a lifelong sense of being inferior across his whole life fits a personality disorder)
x: Autism shows from early childhood with social communication differences and restricted interests, not fear of criticism in someone who wants friends.
Dependent personality disorder centres on needing others to make decisions and fear of being left alone.
Schizoid personality disorder is detachment with no wish for relationships; he wants friends but is afraid.
Social anxiety disorder is fear of particular social or performance situations; a lifelong sense of being inferior across his whole life fits a personality disorder.

hq_q.s: A 34 year old woman's brother died suddenly a month ago. She is tearful, longs for him and sometimes briefly hears his voice when she is falling asleep. She is not sleeping well but is still going to work and looking after her children. She has no thoughts of self-harm.
hq_q.w: Sadness, yearning and even brief sensing or hearing the dead person are common in normal grief, especially early on.
hq_q.f: Intense yearning that disables her for over 6 months → prolonged grief disorder.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most likely diagnosis?

tm.m: Yearning and briefly sensing the dead are part of normal grief
tm.g: Grief with brief sensing of the dead and function kept is a normal grief reaction
f: worthlessness and suicidal thoughts
intense yearning that disables her for over 6 months
the presentation instead showed features specific to Psychotic disorder (Briefly hearing a dead loved one at sleep onset is normal in grief)
the presentation instead showed features specific to PTSD (PTSD needs a traumatic event with flashbacks and avoidance; this is bereavement)
x: Ruled out here: requires worthlessness and suicidal thoughts, whereas this patient has a month ago, briefly hears his voice.
Ruled out here: requires intense yearning that disables her for over 6 months, whereas this patient has a month ago, briefly hears his voice.
Briefly hearing a dead loved one at sleep onset is normal in grief.
PTSD needs a traumatic event with flashbacks and avoidance; this is bereavement.

hq_q.s: A 56 year old woman attends her GP 4 months after her husband died suddenly from a myocardial infarction. She experiences daily waves of intense longing, tearfulness when seeing reminders of him and difficulty concentrating at work, though she maintains her self-care and has no suicidal ideation. Mental state examination shows reactive affect with normal thought form. A diagnosis of normal bereavement versus prolonged grief disorder is considered.
hq_q.w: Under ICD-11, prolonged grief disorder requires persistent, pervasive longing or preoccupation with the deceased accompanied by intense emotional pain that continues for at least 6 months after bereavement, exceeding cultural norms and causing functional impairment.
hq_q.f: Depressed mood, anhedonia and suicidal ideation lasting at least 2 weeks -> depressive episode.
hq_q.ql: What is the minimum duration of symptoms required by ICD-11 to diagnose prolonged grief disorder?

tm.m: Acute bereavement responses normally begin to integrate within 6 months; persistence beyond 6 months with impairment defines prolonged grief disorder.
tm.g: ICD-11 duration threshold for prolonged grief disorder -> 6 months
f: intrusive flashbacks, nightmares and hyperarousal persisting beyond 4 weeks after a traumatic event
pervasive low mood, anhedonia and biological depressive symptoms assessed for major depression
chronic subthreshold depressive symptoms required to diagnose dysthymia in adults
persistent generalized anxiety and worry evaluated for generalized anxiety disorder over several months
x: 1 month is the timeframe within which adjustment disorder or post-traumatic stress disorder is evaluated, not prolonged grief.
2 weeks is the minimum duration required to diagnose a depressive episode in ICD-11, not prolonged grief disorder.
2 years is the minimum duration for dysthymia (persistent depressive disorder), whereas ICD-11 sets 6 months for prolonged grief.
At 3 months after bereavement, intense yearning remains within the expected acute grief period under ICD-11 criteria.

hq_q.s: A 74 year old man's wife died 2 months ago. He now feels worthless and says he is a burden. He has lost all interest in his garden and grandchildren, has stopped eating and has lost 6 kg. He says he should be dead.
hq_q.w: Worthlessness, global loss of interest and suicidal thoughts go beyond grief and suggest depression, which needs treatment and a risk assessment.
hq_q.f: Sadness linked to reminders of his wife with self-esteem intact → grief.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most likely diagnosis?

tm.m: Worthlessness and global loss of interest go beyond grief
tm.g: Worthlessness, global anhedonia and weight loss after a death is a depressive episode
f: the presentation instead showed features specific to Adjustment disorder (Worthlessness and loss of interest meet criteria for depression)
sadness tied to reminders with self-esteem intact
the presentation instead showed features specific to Prolonged grief disorder (Prolonged grief needs at least 6 months; his features are depressive)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Schizophrenia (There are no psychotic symptoms)
x: Worthlessness and loss of interest meet criteria for depression.
Ruled out here: requires sadness tied to reminders with self-esteem intact, whereas this patient has feels worthless, lost all interest.
Prolonged grief needs at least 6 months; his features are depressive.
There are no psychotic symptoms.

hq_q.s:
A 60 year old woman started prednisolone 60 mg daily for giant cell arteritis 5 days ago. She has no psychiatric history. She has become elated, sleepless, talkative and says she has special powers.
Temperature 36.8°C. She is orientated. Thyroid function and glucose are normal.
hq_q.w: High-dose steroids can cause mania or psychosis within days, usually with no past history. Reduce the dose if possible.
hq_q.f: A past history of mood episodes and a family history with no new drug → bipolar disorder.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most likely diagnosis?

tm.m: High-dose steroids can trigger mania or psychosis within days
tm.g: Mania days after high-dose steroids with no history is steroid-induced mania
f: confusion with fever and fluctuating attention
Never give an antidepressant alone in bipolar: it can flip someone into mania.
Third-person voices commenting, thoughts being broadcast, 6 months of decline
the presentation instead showed features specific to Thyrotoxicosis (Thyrotoxicosis does not start 5 days after high-dose steroids with elation)
x: Ruled out here: requires confusion with fever and fluctuating attention, whereas this patient has prednisolone 60 mg, 5 days ago.
Ruled out here: requires Never give an antidepressant alone in bipolar: it can flip someone into mania, whereas this patient has prednisolone 60 mg, 5 days ago.
Ruled out here: requires Third-person voices commenting, thoughts being broadcast, 6 months of decline, whereas this patient has prednisolone 60 mg, 5 days ago.
Thyrotoxicosis does not start 5 days after high-dose steroids with elation.

hq_q.s: A 20 year old man has been brought in by his flatmates because he thinks they are plotting against him and he hears voices. He has smoked large amounts of skunk cannabis daily for 2 weeks. He stops using cannabis in hospital and his symptoms resolve completely within 4 days.
hq_q.w: Drug-induced psychosis settles with abstinence. Persistence beyond about a month suggests a primary psychotic illness.
hq_q.f: Symptoms persist for 3 months despite stopping → schizophrenia.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most likely diagnosis?

tm.m: High-potency THC can cause a short psychosis that settles with abstinence
tm.g: Psychosis resolving within days of stopping cannabis is substance-induced psychosis
f: the presentation instead showed features specific to Bipolar affective disorder (Bipolar disorder needs a mood episode; there is none)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Delusional disorder (Delusional disorder does not resolve within days of stopping cannabis)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Schizoaffective disorder (Schizoaffective disorder needs mood and psychotic symptoms together over time)
symptoms persist for months after stopping
x: Bipolar disorder needs a mood episode; there is none.
Delusional disorder does not resolve within days of stopping cannabis.
Schizoaffective disorder needs mood and psychotic symptoms together over time.
Ruled out here: requires symptoms persist for months after stopping, whereas this patient has skunk cannabis daily, resolve completely within 4 days.

hq_q.s: A 70 year old man with no psychiatric history has developed visual hallucinations of people in his house and believes his neighbours are spying on him. Symptoms started 2 weeks ago.
hq_q.w: New psychosis in older age is usually organic. Check drugs, infection, metabolic causes and do brain imaging.
hq_q.f: A 22-year-old with first-rank symptoms and normal tests → schizophrenia.
hq_q.ql: Which should be done before diagnosing a primary psychosis?

c: 70 year old man with no psychiatric history
tm.m: New psychosis in older age is usually from drugs, delirium or dementia
tm.g: New psychosis in older age: screen for an organic cause first
f: the presentation instead showed features specific to Admit under section 2 (Detention is for those at risk who will not have treatment voluntarily; first find the cause)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Refer for CBT for psychosis (CBT comes after a diagnosis)

the presentation instead showed features specific to Start a cholinesterase inhibitor (Hallucinations in an older person can be Lewy body dementia, which may respond to a cholinesterase inhibitor, but delirium and other organic causes must be excluded first)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Start an antipsychotic (Antipsychotics are risky in older people and may hide an organic cause)
x: Detention is for those at risk who will not have treatment voluntarily; first find the cause.
CBT comes after a diagnosis.
Hallucinations in an older person can be Lewy body dementia, which may respond to a cholinesterase inhibitor, but delirium and other organic causes must be excluded first.
Antipsychotics are risky in older people and may hide an organic cause.

hq_q.s: A 65 year old man presents with a 3-month history of intensely itchy, weeping patches on both lower legs that worsened during the winter months. He has a background of generalized xerosis. Examination reveals four well-demarcated, coin-shaped erythematous plaques measuring 3 cm across on both shins, with surface crusting, pinpoint vesicles and no central clearing. Microscopy of potassium hydroxide skin scrapings is negative for fungal hyphae.
hq_q.w: Discoid (nummular) eczema presents with well-demarcated, coin-shaped erythematous plaques that are often vesicular, weeping and crusted on the limbs of older adults with dry skin. Negative skin scrapings exclude tinea corporis.
hq_q.f: Annular scaly plaque with central clearing and positive KOH microscopy -> tinea corporis.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most likely diagnosis?

tm.m: Impaired epidermal barrier function triggers focal spongiotic dermatitis forming circular nummular plaques.
tm.g: Coin-shaped weeping vesicular plaques on dry shins with negative fungal scrapings -> Discoid eczema
f: itchy purple flat-topped papules on the flexor wrists with lacy white buccal mucosal striae
a single oval herald patch followed by fine collarette-scaled macules along skin cleavage lines on the trunk
well-demarcated red plaques covered in thick silvery scale on the extensor elbows and knees
an expanding annular plaque with central clearing and branching septate hyphae on skin scrapings
x: Lichen planus presents with violaceous, flat-topped polygonal papules with Wickham's striae on the flexor wrists rather than weeping nummular plaques.
Pityriasis rosea starts with a single herald patch followed by oval salmon-pink macules in a fir-tree distribution on the trunk.
Plaque psoriasis causes dry, well-demarcated erythematous plaques with thick silvery scale on extensor surfaces, not weeping vesicular lesions.
Tinea corporis produces asymmetrical annular plaques with an active scaly border, central clearing and fungal hyphae on skin scrapings.

hq_q.s: A 32 year old woman presents with a 3-week history of intensely itchy, tiny blisters across her palms and the sides of her fingers. Episodes flare in warm summer weather and during work stress. She has seasonal allergic rhinitis. Examination shows clusters of deep-seated, clear tapioca-like vesicles and peeling along the lateral aspects of the digits and palms, sparing the finger web spaces and wrists.
hq_q.w: Pompholyx (dyshidrotic eczema) is an acute vesicular palmoplantar dermatitis characterised by intensely pruritic, deep-seated 'tapioca-like' vesicles along the lateral aspects of the fingers and palms, often triggered by heat, hyperhidrosis or stress.
hq_q.f: Linear burrows in the finger web spaces with nocturnal itch affecting family members -> palmar scabies infestation.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most likely diagnosis?

tm.m: Acute spongiotic inflammation trapped beneath the thick stratum corneum of the palms forms deep-seated tapioca vesicles.
tm.g: Deep-seated itchy vesicles on the palms and lateral finger borders sparing web spaces -> Pompholyx
f: intensely itchy grouped vesicles on the elbows and buttocks in a patient with coeliac disease
painful oral mucosal ulcers with tender oval vesicles on the palms and soles in a febrile child
serpiginous burrows in the finger web spaces and flexor wrists with severe nocturnal itch in household contacts
unilateral dry palmar scaling with a raised border alongside bilateral moccasin-distribution tinea pedis
x: Dermatitis herpetiformis causes grouped excoriated vesicles over the extensor elbows, knees and buttocks associated with coeliac disease.
Hand, foot and mouth disease causes painful oral ulcers and tender erythematous maculopapular vesicles on the hands and feet with viral prodrome.
Scabies affects the finger web spaces and flexor wrists with linear burrows and nocturnal pruritus affecting household contacts.
Tinea manuum typically causes unilateral diffuse palmar hyperkeratosis and fine scaling in the 'two feet, one hand' pattern rather than bilateral deep vesicles.

hq_q.s: A 38 year old man presents with a 4-week flare of pompholyx affecting both palms, causing intense pruritus and painful fissuring that interferes with his manual job. Frequent application of greasy emollients and soap substitutes has failed to control the flare. Examination shows crops of intact deep-seated vesicles and erythema over the thick palmar skin of both hands, with no weeping yellow crusting or spreading cellulitis.
hq_q.w: NICE recommends a short course (2 to 4 weeks) of a potent or very potent topical corticosteroid, such as clobetasol propionate 0.05%, alongside regular emollients for severe palmoplantar eczema because the thick stratum corneum resists milder preparations.
hq_q.f: Mild facial or eyelid eczema flare -> hydrocortisone acetate 1%.
hq_q.ql: Which topical corticosteroid is most appropriate to prescribe for this acute flare?

c: emollients and soap substitutes has failed
tm.m: The thick palmar stratum corneum requires a very potent topical corticosteroid to achieve anti-inflammatory penetration.
tm.g: Refractory pompholyx on thick palmar skin -> Clobetasol propionate 0.05%
f: moderate-potency topical steroid step-down therapy for trunk eczema in a child
short course of moderate-potency topical steroid for mild flexural eczema on the neck
mild corticosteroid therapy for a localized patch of subacute dermatitis on thin skin
first-line mild topical corticosteroid for atopic eczema affecting the face or eyelids
x: Betamethasone valerate 0.025% (1 in 4 dilution) is only moderate potency and is insufficient to penetrate thick palmar stratum corneum.
Clobetasone butyrate 0.05% is a moderate-potency steroid suited for delicate sites or mild limb flares rather than severe palmar pompholyx.
Fludroxycortide 0.0125% cream is a mild-to-moderate corticosteroid that cannot penetrate hyperkeratotic palmar skin in acute pompholyx.
Hydrocortisone 1% is a mild corticosteroid used on the face, eyelids or flexures and is ineffective on thick palmar skin.

hq_q.s: A 45 year old woman presents with a 3-month history of purulent nasal crusting, recurrent epistaxis and progressive malaise, followed by 4 days of haemoptysis. Temperature is 37.6°C, pulse rate 94 bpm and BP 158/94 mmHg. Examination reveals a saddle-nose deformity. Urine dipstick shows blood 3+ and protein 2+. Serum creatinine is 198 µmol/L (60–120), and chest X-ray demonstrates multiple bilateral cavitating pulmonary nodules.
hq_q.w: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA) is a small-vessel necrotising granulomatous vasculitis causing upper airway destruction (epistaxis, saddle nose), cavitating pulmonary nodules and pauci-immune glomerulonephritis. Cytoplasmic ANCA (c-ANCA) directed against proteinase-3 (PR3) is positive in ~90% of generalised disease.
hq_q.f: Late-onset asthma, eosinophilia and mononeuritis multiplex -> p-ANCA against MPO (EGPA).
hq_q.ql: Which autoantibody is most likely to be positive?

tm.m: Autoantibodies against neutrophil proteinase-3 activate neutrophils, driving necrotising granulomatous small-vessel vasculitis.
tm.g: Saddle nose, cavitating lung nodules and rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis -> c-ANCA against PR3
f: malar rash, photosensitivity, low complement C3/C4 and immune-complex lupus nephritis
pulmonary haemorrhage and crescentic glomerulonephritis with linear IgG on renal biopsy and no sinus disease
Raynaud's phenomenon, puffy fingers, arthralgia and myositis in mixed connective tissue disease
late-onset asthma, peripheral blood eosinophilia and mononeuritis multiplex in EGPA
x: Anti-dsDNA and anti-C1q antibodies are specific for systemic lupus erythematosus with lupus nephritis rather than necrotising granulomatous vasculitis.
Anti-GBM antibodies against type IV collagen cause Goodpasture disease with diffuse alveolar haemorrhage and linear IgG staining, without nasal destruction.
Anti-U1-RNP antibodies are characteristic of mixed connective tissue disease presenting with Raynaud's phenomenon, swollen fingers and myositis.
p-ANCA against myeloperoxidase is predominantly associated with microscopic polyangiitis and eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis rather than cavitating GPA.

hq_q.s: A 54 year old man with PR3-ANCA-positive granulomatosis with polyangiitis is admitted with fatigue and ankle oedema. Over 2 weeks his serum creatinine has risen from 110 µmol/L to 240 µmol/L (60–120). BP is 164/96 mmHg. Urine microscopy shows dysmorphic erythrocytes and red cell casts. Urgent renal biopsy demonstrates pauci-immune necrotising crescentic glomerulonephritis affecting 60% of sampled glomeruli.
hq_q.w: Organ-threatening or life-threatening ANCA-associated vasculitis, including rapidly progressive pauci-immune crescentic glomerulonephritis, requires urgent remission induction with high-dose corticosteroids combined with either rituximab or pulsed intravenous cyclophosphamide.
hq_q.f: Remission maintenance after induction has controlled the acute nephritis -> azathioprine with low-dose prednisolone.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most appropriate remission-induction regimen?

c: creatinine has risen from 110 µmol/L to 240 µmol/L
tm.m: B-cell depletion with rituximab plus high-dose glucocorticoids halts ANCA-mediated necrotising glomerular inflammation.
tm.g: GPA with crescentic glomerulonephritis -> High-dose steroids with rituximab (or cyclophosphamide)
f: remission maintenance therapy after successful cyclophosphamide or rituximab induction
giant cell arteritis without small-vessel renal or pulmonary involvement
Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia prophylaxis in a patient receiving rituximab or cyclophosphamide
non-organ-threatening upper airway disease with normal renal function and no glomerulonephritis
x: Azathioprine with low-dose prednisolone is used for remission maintenance after induction, not for acute organ-threatening crescentic nephritis.
Corticosteroid monotherapy fails to halt rapidly progressive ANCA-associated glomerulonephritis and carries high mortality without rituximab or cyclophosphamide.
Co-trimoxazole is used for Pneumocystis prophylaxis alongside immunosuppression, not as induction therapy for crescentic glomerulonephritis.
Methotrexate may be considered in non-organ-threatening nasal disease with normal renal function, but is contraindicated and inadequate in severe renal failure.

hq_q.s:
An 8 year old boy has a rash on his legs and buttocks, painful ankles and colicky abdominal pain. He had a cold a week ago.
Temperature 37.4°C, BP 104/66 mmHg. There is raised, palpable purpura on the buttocks and the backs of the legs. Both ankles are swollen. Urine dipstick shows blood 1+.
Platelet count is normal.
hq_q.w: IgA vasculitis, Henoch-Schönlein purpura: palpable purpura on the legs and buttocks with joint, gut and kidney involvement. Platelets are normal.
hq_q.f: Fever, non-blanching rash and an unwell child → meningococcal sepsis, IM benzylpenicillin.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most likely diagnosis?

tm.m: IgA immune complexes inflame small vessels in skin, joints, gut and kidney
tm.g: Palpable purpura with arthritis and abdominal pain after a cold is IgA vasculitis
f: the presentation instead showed features specific to GPA (GPA affects adults with sinus, lung and kidney disease, not a child with purpura and joint pain)
5 days of fever with red eyes and cracked lips
bruising with a low platelet count and pallor
a spreading non-blanching rash in an unwell febrile child
x: GPA affects adults with sinus, lung and kidney disease, not a child with purpura and joint pain.
Ruled out here: requires 5 days of fever with red eyes and cracked lips, whereas this patient has cold a week ago, palpable purpura on the buttocks.
Ruled out here: requires bruising with a low platelet count and pallor, whereas this patient has cold a week ago, palpable purpura on the buttocks.
Ruled out here: requires a spreading non-blanching rash in an unwell febrile child, whereas this patient has cold a week ago, palpable purpura on the buttocks.

hq_q.s: A 68 year old man has a tumour of the caecum. He is listed for a right hemicolectomy, and the surgeon plans to divide the main artery to the tumour at its origin.
hq_q.w: The SMA gives the ileocolic, right colic and middle colic arteries, supplying up to two thirds of the transverse colon.
hq_q.f: Descending colon → left colic artery, from the IMA.
hq_q.ql: Which artery mainly supplies the caecum?

tm.m: The superior mesenteric artery gives the ileocolic branch to the caecum
tm.g: The caecum and ascending colon are supplied by the ileocolic artery
f: short stature and primary amenorrhoea + webbed neck
the descending colon
the transverse colon

the presentation instead showed features specific to Right colic artery (The right colic artery supplies the ascending colon above the caecum and is often absent; the caecum is fed by the ileocolic artery)
x: Ruled out here: requires short stature and primary amenorrhoea + webbed neck, whereas this patient has tumour of the caecum, right hemicolectomy.
Ruled out here: requires the descending colon, whereas this patient has tumour of the caecum, right hemicolectomy.
Ruled out here: requires the transverse colon, whereas this patient has tumour of the caecum, right hemicolectomy.
The right colic artery supplies the ascending colon above the caecum and is often absent; the caecum is fed by the ileocolic artery.

hq_q.s: A 76 year old woman with heart failure has had left-sided abdominal pain and bloody diarrhoea after an episode of low blood pressure. Colonoscopy shows ischaemic colitis in a watershed area between two arterial territories.
hq_q.w: The splenic flexure lies between SMA and IMA territories, Griffiths point, so low flow hits it first.
hq_q.f: The rectosigmoid junction → Sudeck's point, the other watershed.
hq_q.ql: Which part of the colon is a watershed area most prone to ischaemia?

tm.m: The splenic flexure sits at the edge of both the SMA and IMA territories
tm.g: The splenic flexure is the classic watershed area
f: the presentation instead showed features specific to Caecum (The caecum is not the classic watershed area)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Hepatic flexure (Supplied well by the middle and right colic branches of the SMA)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Rectum (Dual blood supply from inferior mesenteric and internal iliac arteries spares the rectum)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Sigmoid colon (The sigmoid is a common site of diverticula, but the splenic flexure is the watershed)
x: The caecum is not the classic watershed area.
Supplied well by the middle and right colic branches of the SMA
Dual blood supply from inferior mesenteric and internal iliac arteries spares the rectum
The sigmoid is a common site of diverticula, but the splenic flexure is the watershed.

hq_q.s: An 80 year old woman with untreated atrial fibrillation presents with a 5-hour history of sudden, severe central abdominal pain out of proportion to examination findings. Pulse rate is 118 bpm irregularly irregular and BP 106/68 mmHg. Arterial lactate is 4.8 mmol/L (<2.0). Urgent CT mesenteric angiography shows an embolus occluding the superior mesenteric artery just distal to the origin of the middle colic artery.
hq_q.w: Superior mesenteric artery emboli classically lodge just distal to the origin of the middle colic artery, sparing the proximal jejunal and middle colic branches while rendering the main jejunum, ileum, caecum and ascending (right) colon ischaemic.
hq_q.f: Occlusion of the inferior mesenteric artery -> descending and sigmoid colon ischaemia.
hq_q.ql: Which segment of the gastrointestinal tract is most likely to become ischaemic?

c: just distal to the origin of the middle colic artery
tm.m: An embolus lodging distal to the middle colic takeoff occludes the jejunal, ileal, ileocolic and right colic branches.
tm.g: SMA embolus distal to the middle colic artery -> Jejunum, ileum and right colon
f: thrombotic occlusion of the inferior mesenteric artery at its aortic origin
bilateral internal iliac artery embolisation causing pelvic and lower rectal ischaemia
selective occlusion of the middle colic branch of the superior mesenteric artery
thrombotic occlusion of the coeliac axis with failed collateral flow
x: The descending and sigmoid colon are supplied by the inferior mesenteric artery rather than the superior mesenteric artery.
The lower rectum receives blood from the middle and inferior rectal branches of the internal iliac and internal pudendal arteries.
Because the embolus lodged distal to the middle colic artery origin, blood flow to the transverse colon is preserved.
The stomach and proximal duodenum are supplied by the coeliac trunk and its rich collateral arcade, not the superior mesenteric artery.

hq_q.s: A 28 year old man presents with a 4-week history of a painless, firm swelling in his right testicle. Scrotal ultrasound demonstrates a well-defined 2.8 cm hypoechoic intratesticular mass, and serum beta-hCG is elevated. He undergoes a radical inguinal orchidectomy confirming a non-seminomatous germ cell tumour, with no invasion of the scrotal skin. A staging contrast CT scan of the thorax, abdomen and pelvis is performed.
hq_q.w: Because the testes originate in the posterior abdominal wall near the developing kidneys and descend through the inguinal canal, their lymphatic vessels accompany the testicular vessels directly to the lumbar para-aortic lymph nodes at the level of L1–L2.
hq_q.f: Tumour invading the scrotal skin -> superficial inguinal lymph nodes.
hq_q.ql: Which lymph node group is the primary site of lymphatic drainage for this tumour?

c: no invasion of the scrotal skin
tm.m: Embryological descent from the retroperitoneum means testicular lymphatics follow the gonadal vessels to the para-aortic nodes.
tm.g: Testicular parenchymal tumour -> Para-aortic lymph nodes
f: squamous cell carcinoma of the glans penis metastasising to deep groin nodes
adenocarcinoma of the prostate or superior bladder wall spreading to pelvic nodes
carcinoma of the uterine cervix or middle rectum spreading to pelvic sidewall nodes
squamous cell carcinoma invading the scrotal skin or lower anal canal below the dentate line
x: Deep inguinal nodes receive lymph from the glans penis and deep lower limb lymphatics rather than the testis.
External iliac nodes drain the bladder, prostate and upper vagina, only involved in testicular cancer after retrograde spread or prior groin surgery.
Internal iliac nodes drain the pelvic viscera, lower rectum above the dentate line and cervix rather than the gonad.
Superficial inguinal nodes drain the scrotal skin and lower anal canal; the testis itself drains upward along the gonadal vessels.

hq_q.s: A 62 year old woman presents with a 3-month history of painful defaecation, fresh rectal bleeding and a persistent ulcerated lump at the anal margin. Proctoscopy and biopsy confirm a 2.5 cm squamous cell carcinoma of the lower anal canal arising entirely below the dentate line. Clinical examination and staging pelvic MRI are arranged to assess regional nodal spread.
hq_q.w: The dentate (pectinate) line marks the embryological junction between endoderm and ectoderm. Tumours arising below the dentate line have somatic innervation and drain via cutaneous lymphatics primarily to the superficial inguinal lymph nodes.
hq_q.f: Adenocarcinoma arising above the dentate line -> internal iliac and inferior mesenteric nodes.
hq_q.ql: Which lymph node group is the primary site of lymphatic drainage for a lesion at this anatomical level?

c: squamous cell carcinoma of the lower anal canal
tm.m: Ectoderm-derived epithelium below the dentate line shares lymphatic drainage with the perianal skin to the superficial inguinal nodes.
tm.g: Anal canal lesion below the dentate line -> Superficial inguinal nodes
f: secondary nodal extension after extensive superficial inguinal lymphadenopathy
adenocarcinoma of the upper rectum or sigmoid colon arising above the dentate line
malignancy of the upper anal canal arising superior to the pectinate (dentate) line
metastatic spread from a primary ovarian or testicular germ cell tumour
x: Deep inguinal (femoral) nodes receive secondary drainage after the superficial inguinal nodes or directly from the glans clitoris.
Inferior mesenteric nodes drain the hindgut derivatives of the upper rectum and sigmoid colon above the dentate line.
Internal iliac nodes drain the upper anal canal and lower rectum above the dentate line rather than the ectodermal lower anal canal.
Para-aortic nodes drain the gonads, kidneys and posterior abdominal wall rather than the perianal skin and lower anal canal.

hq_q.s: A 66 year old woman has a hard, painless, enlarged lymph node above her left clavicle. She has lost 5 kg and has had indigestion and early fullness for 3 months.
hq_q.w: Virchow's node, Troisier's sign: the thoracic duct drains into the left subclavian vein near this node, so abdominal cancers spread there.
hq_q.f: A right supraclavicular node → lung or oesophageal cancer.
hq_q.ql: Which cancer should be considered?

tm.m: The thoracic duct drains into the left neck, so abdominal cancers spread to the left supraclavicular node
tm.g: A left supraclavicular node with dyspepsia and weight loss suggests gastric cancer
f: the presentation instead showed features specific to Breast cancer (Breast cancer spreads to axillary nodes, and she has gastric symptoms)
night sweats with rubbery nodes in a young adult
a hoarse voice in a heavy smoker
the presentation instead showed features specific to Thyroid cancer (Thyroid cancer gives a neck lump, not dyspepsia with weight loss)
x: Breast cancer spreads to axillary nodes, and she has gastric symptoms.
Ruled out here: requires night sweats with rubbery nodes in a young adult, whereas this patient has above her left clavicle, lost 5 kg.
Ruled out here: requires a hoarse voice in a heavy smoker, whereas this patient has above her left clavicle, lost 5 kg.
Thyroid cancer gives a neck lump, not dyspepsia with weight loss.

hq_q.s: A 54 year old woman stopped her long-term oral prednisolone for polymyalgia rheumatica abruptly 2 weeks ago after running out of tablets on holiday. She now presents with severe lethargy, anorexia, nausea and postural lightheadedness. Temperature is 36.6°C and pulse rate 88 bpm. Blood pressure is 94/58 mmHg lying and 78/50 mmHg standing. Serum sodium is 128 mmol/L (135–146) and glucose 3.8 mmol/L (4.0–7.8).
hq_q.w: The short synacthen (tetracosactide 250 micrograms) stimulation test is the definitive diagnostic test for adrenal insufficiency, measuring serum cortisol at 0 and 30 minutes. Failure of cortisol to rise above the local threshold confirms inadequate adrenal reserve.
hq_q.f: Suspected Cushing's syndrome with proximal myopathy and striae -> low-dose dexamethasone suppression test.
hq_q.ql: Which investigation is the gold standard to confirm suspected adrenal insufficiency?

tm.m: Prolonged exogenous glucocorticoid therapy suppresses CRH and ACTH, causing adrenal cortical atrophy and blunted response to synacthen.
tm.g: Suspected adrenal insufficiency -> Short synacthen test
f: paroxysmal headaches, sweating, palpitations and severe labile hypertension
proximal myopathy, purple abdominal striae, moon facies and suspected Cushing's syndrome
loss of circadian cortisol nadir in a patient with suspected endogenous hypercortisolism
resistant hypertension accompanied by unprovoked hypokalaemia and metabolic alkalosis
x: Urinary metanephrines are used to screen for catecholamine-secreting phaeochromocytoma in episodic hypertension, not adrenal insufficiency.
The overnight or low-dose dexamethasone suppression test investigates suspected cortisol excess (Cushing's syndrome), not hypocortisolaemia.
Late-night salivary or serum cortisol assesses loss of diurnal rhythm in Cushing's syndrome rather than adrenal insufficiency.
The aldosterone-to-renin ratio screens for primary hyperaldosteronism (Conn's syndrome) in hypertension with hypokalaemia.

hq_q.s:
A 44 year old man has had fatigue and weight loss for 3 months and Addison's disease is suspected. He is not acutely unwell and takes no steroids or oestrogens. A blood test is taken at 9 am.
BP 128/78 mmHg.
hq_q.w: A 9 am cortisol above about 500 nmol/L makes adrenal insufficiency very unlikely, so no synacthen test is needed. Below about 100 nmol/L makes it likely; values in between need a short synacthen test.
hq_q.f: 9 am cortisol of 80 nmol/L with low sodium and high potassium → Addison's likely; urgent short synacthen test and specialist referral.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most appropriate interpretation?
hq_q.post: His 9am cortisol is 600 nmol/L (200–700).

tm.m: Cortisol peaks in the early morning, so a high 9 am value shows the adrenals can make plenty
tm.g: 9 am cortisol over 500: Addison's very unlikely
f: the presentation instead showed features specific to Addison's is confirmed (A high-normal cortisol argues against Addison's; diagnosis needs a low cortisol that fails to rise on synacthen)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Needs a short synacthen test (A synacthen test is for an equivocal 9 am cortisol (roughly 100 to 500 nmol/L), not a clearly high one)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Repeat at midnight to confirm (A late-night cortisol screens for Cushing's syndrome, not adrenal insufficiency)

the presentation instead showed features specific to Suggests Cushing's syndrome (A single normal morning cortisol does not suggest Cushing's, which needs a dexamethasone suppression or late-night cortisol test)
x: A high-normal cortisol argues against Addison's; diagnosis needs a low cortisol that fails to rise on synacthen.
A synacthen test is for an equivocal 9 am cortisol (roughly 100 to 500 nmol/L), not a clearly high one.
A late-night cortisol screens for Cushing's syndrome, not adrenal insufficiency.
A single normal morning cortisol does not suggest Cushing's, which needs a dexamethasone suppression or late-night cortisol test.

hq_q.s: A 48 year old woman presents with a 4-month history of progressive fatigue, 6 kg weight loss, salt craving and postural dizziness. Examination reveals hyperpigmentation of the palmar creases and buccal mucosa, with a blood pressure of 96/60 mmHg. A short synacthen test shows a baseline 9 am cortisol of 82 nmol/L and a 30-minute cortisol of 110 nmol/L, confirming adrenal insufficiency.
hq_q.w: In primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison's disease), loss of cortisol negative feedback drives pituitary corticotrophs to secrete high levels of ACTH and pro-opiomelanocortin, causing mucosal hyperpigmentation. In secondary pituitary insufficiency, plasma ACTH is low or inappropriately normal.
hq_q.f: Low plasma ACTH with absent hyperpigmentation and preserved aldosterone -> secondary pituitary adrenal insufficiency.
hq_q.ql: Which biochemical finding best distinguishes primary adrenal failure from secondary pituitary insufficiency?

c: hyperpigmentation of the palmar creases and buccal mucosa
tm.m: Loss of adrenal cortisol feedback stimulates pituitary POMC and ACTH hypersecretion in primary adrenal failure.
tm.g: Distinguishing primary from secondary adrenal insufficiency -> High morning plasma ACTH
f: assessing severity of glucocorticoid deficiency rather than localising the axis level
initial screening before dynamic testing in any form of hypocortisolaemia
confirming impaired adrenal cortical reserve without differentiating primary from chronic secondary disease
evaluating electrolyte disturbance present in both primary and secondary hypocortisolaemia
x: Hypoglycaemia due to loss of cortisol counter-regulation occurs in both primary adrenal failure and secondary ACTH deficiency.
A low morning serum cortisol is present in both primary adrenal cortex destruction and secondary pituitary ACTH failure.
In chronic secondary adrenal insufficiency, prolonged ACTH deprivation causes adrenal atrophy, so both primary and chronic secondary failure fail the synacthen test.
Hyponatraemia occurs in both primary adrenal failure (aldosterone and cortisol loss) and secondary failure (cortisol deficiency causing ADH hypersecretion).

hq_q.s:
A 78 year old woman has had two falls in a month after feeling dizzy when standing up.
Her BP is 142/80 mmHg lying and 115/72 mmHg after 3 minutes standing. Her pulse rate rises from 70 to 78 bpm.
hq_q.w: A fall of 20 systolic or 10 diastolic within 3 minutes of standing is orthostatic hypotension.
hq_q.f: Drop of 10 systolic only → not orthostatic hypotension.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most likely diagnosis?

c: 142/80 mmHg lying and 115/72 mmHg after 3 minutes standing
tm.m: A drop of 20 systolic or 10 diastolic within 3 minutes defines orthostatic hypotension
tm.g: A 27 mmHg systolic fall on standing is orthostatic hypotension
f: the presentation instead showed features specific to Hypertension (Her lying BP is normal; the 27 mmHg fall on standing is the finding)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Normal age-related change (A fall of 27 mmHg systolic on standing is not a normal age change; 20 or more is orthostatic hypotension)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Vasovagal response (A vasovagal response causes bradycardia and faints)
the presentation instead showed features specific to White coat effect (The white coat effect raises readings in clinic)
x: Her lying BP is normal; the 27 mmHg fall on standing is the finding.
A fall of 27 mmHg systolic on standing is not a normal age change; 20 or more is orthostatic hypotension.
A vasovagal response causes bradycardia and faints.
The white coat effect raises readings in clinic.

hq_q.s: An 82 year old man presents after three falls in 2 months, each occurring shortly after standing up from his chair. He takes doxazosin 4 mg daily for lower urinary tract symptoms, plus amlodipine 5 mg, ramipril 5 mg and furosemide 20 mg daily. Blood pressure is 148/78 mmHg lying and 118/64 mmHg after 3 minutes of standing, with pulse 74 bpm and no oedema.
o: Start midodrine 2.5 mg three times daily
hq_q.w: NICE falls guidance defines postural hypotension as a systolic drop >=20 mmHg or diastolic drop >=10 mmHg within 3 minutes of standing and prioritises medication review first. Alpha-1 blockers such as doxazosin are a leading reversible cause.
hq_q.f: Neurogenic orthostatic hypotension in Parkinson's disease with no culprit drugs -> fluid/salt loading, then midodrine or fludrocortisone.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most appropriate initial step in management?

c: 148/78 mmHg lying and 118/64 mmHg after 3 minutes of standing
tm.m: Alpha-1 adrenoceptor blockade prevents reflex peripheral arteriolar constriction on standing, causing venous pooling and postural hypotension.
tm.g: Symptomatic orthostatic hypotension in a patient taking an alpha-blocker -> Stop doxazosin therapy
f: persistent neurogenic orthostatic hypotension after all culprit vasodilators have been stopped
primary autonomic failure with persistent orthostatic syncope despite conservative measures and drug review
severe autonomic failure in multiple system atrophy refractory to medication withdrawal and fluid loading
acute kidney injury with a creatinine rise exceeding 30% or hyperkalaemia on an ACE inhibitor
x: Non-pharmacological compression hosiery is secondary to withdrawing reversible culprit medications causing orthostatic hypotension.
Adding a mineralocorticoid to treat drug-induced postural hypotension is inappropriate before stopping the causative alpha-blocker, especially in hypertension.
Midodrine is an alpha-1 agonist reserved for refractory neurogenic orthostatic hypotension; giving it while continuing an alpha-1 blocker is pharmacological antagonism.
Alpha-1 blockers such as doxazosin are the prime culprits for acute orthostatic blood pressure drops and should be withdrawn before prognostic antihypertensives.

hq_q.s: A 68 year old woman presents with a 2-month history of bilateral ankle swelling that worsens by evening. Her hypertension is controlled on amlodipine 10 mg daily and indapamide 2.5 mg daily. She has no orthopnoea or dyspnoea. Blood pressure is 132/78 mmHg, pulse 72 bpm and JVP is not raised. Pitting oedema extends to the mid-shins. Serum albumin, creatinine and urine dipstick are normal.
o: Add oral furosemide 40 mg every morning
Double the daily dose of oral indapamide
Replace amlodipine with an ACE inhibitor
hq_q.w: Dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers (especially amlodipine 10 mg) selectively dilate precapillary arterioles more than postcapillary venules, raising capillary hydrostatic pressure and causing ankle oedema. Diuretics are ineffective; switching to an ACE inhibitor or ARB resolves it.
hq_q.f: Symptomatic hyponatraemia or gout precipitated by thiazide therapy -> stop indapamide.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most appropriate adjustment to her antihypertensive regimen?

c: Pitting oedema extends to the mid-shins
albumin, creatinine and urine dipstick are normal
tm.m: Selective precapillary arteriolar vasodilation increases intracapillary hydrostatic pressure, driving fluid into the interstitium independently of sodium retention.
tm.g: Bilateral ankle oedema on high-dose amlodipine with normal JVP and albumin -> Replace amlodipine with an ACE inhibitor
f: fluid overload with raised JVP and pulmonary crackles due to decompensated heart failure
inadequate blood pressure control on submaximal thiazide therapy without vasodilatory oedema
chronic venous eczema, haemosiderin pigmentation and varicose veins with normal arterial Doppler
symptomatic hyponatraemia, gout flare or postural hypotension attributed to thiazide-like diuretic therapy
x: Loop diuretics do not correct precapillary vasodilatory oedema from dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers and cause unnecessary electrolyte loss.
Increasing thiazide-like diuretic dose increases hypokalaemia and hyponatraemia risk without resolving calcium channel blocker-induced capillary hydrostatic oedema.
Compression stockings treat chronic venous insufficiency rather than drug-induced precapillary arteriolar vasodilation from high-dose amlodipine.
Indapamide is a thiazide-like diuretic that does not cause peripheral oedema; stopping it leaves the causative amlodipine 10 mg in place.

hq_q.s: A 62 year old man with a 12-year history of poorly controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus presents with a 6-month history of bilateral burning foot pain and intermittent electric-shock sensations that disturb his sleep. Contact with bedsheets triggers severe discomfort. Examination reveals reduced pinprick and vibration sensation in a stocking distribution to the mid-calves and absent ankle reflexes bilaterally, with palpable dorsalis pedis pulses.
hq_q.w: Neuropathic pain arises from a lesion or disease of the somatosensory nervous system, characterised by burning or shooting electric-shock sensations, paraesthesia, allodynia (pain from non-painful stimuli such as bedsheets) and sensory deficit. NICE recommends amitriptyline, duloxetine, gabapentin or pregabalin first-line.
hq_q.f: Localized aching knee pain worse on weight-bearing with bony crepitus -> nociceptive somatic pain.
hq_q.ql: Which pathophysiological category of pain best describes his presentation?

c: Contact with bedsheets triggers severe discomfort
tm.m: Chronic hyperglycaemic microvascular injury to small nociceptive C-fibres causes ectopic spontaneous firing and central sensitisation.
tm.g: Burning, electric-shock pain with tactile allodynia and stocking sensory loss -> Neuropathic pain
f: well-localized aching joint pain worse on weight-bearing in knee osteoarthritis
widespread musculoskeletal pain, fatigue and unrefreshing sleep with normal neurological examination in fibromyalgia
right shoulder tip pain arising from diaphragmatic irritation by a subphrenic collection
poorly localized central colicky abdominal pain with sweating and nausea in small bowel obstruction
x: Nociceptive somatic pain arises from tissue injury activating intact nociceptors, causing a localized aching or throbbing pain without allodynia or sensory loss.
Nociplastic pain occurs in conditions like fibromyalgia with widespread pain and normal peripheral nerve function rather than length-dependent axonal neuropathy.
Referred pain is perceived at a site distant from the primary lesion sharing spinal segmental innervation, without distal stocking sensory loss.
Visceral pain originates from internal organs, producing poorly localized deep cramping or colicky pain with autonomic features rather than burning foot allodynia.

hq_q.s:
A 44 year old man had a laparoscopic cholecystectomy yesterday. He now has pain at the tip of his right shoulder.
His shoulder has a full range of movement and is not tender.
hq_q.w: Gas irritates the diaphragm, supplied by C3 to C5 through the phrenic nerve, which shares a dermatome with the shoulder tip.
hq_q.f: Pain around the umbilicus early in appendicitis → visceral pain from midgut.
hq_q.ql: Which type of pain is this?

tm.m: Gas irritates the diaphragm, supplied by C3 to C5, which also supply the shoulder skin
tm.g: Shoulder tip pain after laparoscopy is referred pain from the diaphragm
f: lost light touch and pin prick, ulcer under a pressure point, normal ABPI
pain felt in a limb that has been amputated
the presentation instead showed features specific to Port-site wound pain (Port-site pain is felt at the wounds on the abdomen, not at the tip of the shoulder)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Shoulder strain from positioning (Positioning strain gives a tender shoulder with painful movement; his shoulder moves fully and is not tender)
x: Ruled out here: requires lost light touch and pin prick, ulcer under a pressure point, normal ABPI, whereas this patient has laparoscopic cholecystectomy yesterday, tip of his right shoulder.
Ruled out here: requires pain felt in a limb that has been amputated, whereas this patient has laparoscopic cholecystectomy yesterday, tip of his right shoulder.
Port-site pain is felt at the wounds on the abdomen, not at the tip of the shoulder.
Positioning strain gives a tender shoulder with painful movement; his shoulder moves fully and is not tender.

hq_q.s:
A 48 year old man has had low back pain for 6 weeks after lifting. The pain spreads vaguely into his left buttock and the back of his thigh but not below the knee. He has no numbness, weakness or bladder symptoms.
Straight leg raise is negative. Neurological examination of the legs is normal.
hq_q.w: Somatic referred pain from spinal structures spreads vaguely into the buttock and thigh. Radicular pain follows a dermatome below the knee.
hq_q.f: Shooting pain below the knee in a dermatome with a positive straight leg raise → radicular.
hq_q.ql: Which type of pain is this?

tm.m: Pain from spinal joints and discs spreads vaguely without a nerve root pattern
tm.g: Vague buttock and thigh pain above the knee with normal neurology is somatic referred pain
f: the presentation instead showed features specific to Malingering (Nothing suggests deliberate faking)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Neuropathic pain (Neuropathic pain is burning or shooting below the knee with signs; his neurology is normal)
shooting pain below the knee in a dermatome with a positive straight leg raise
the presentation instead showed features specific to Visceral pain (Visceral pain comes from organs, not the lumbar structures after lifting)
x: Nothing suggests deliberate faking.
Neuropathic pain is burning or shooting below the knee with signs; his neurology is normal.
Ruled out here: requires shooting pain below the knee in a dermatome with a positive straight leg raise, whereas this patient has not below the knee, no numbness, weakness.
Visceral pain comes from organs, not the lumbar structures after lifting.

hq_q.s:
A 24 year old man has had a blocked, runny nose with sneezing and itchy eyes every summer for 5 years. This year his symptoms have lasted 6 weeks and disturb his sleep. Oral cetirizine has helped only a little.
The nasal mucosa is pale and swollen. There are no nasal polyps.
hq_q.w: Intranasal steroids are the most effective treatment for persistent allergic rhinitis. Start before the pollen season.
hq_q.f: Occasional mild symptoms → an oral non-sedating antihistamine as needed.
hq_q.ql: Which treatment is most effective for persistent symptoms?

c: cetirizine has helped only a little
tm.m: Intranasal steroids reduce allergic inflammation in the nose
tm.g: Persistent allergic rhinitis: intranasal corticosteroid
f: the presentation instead showed features specific to Intranasal antihistamine (An intranasal antihistamine such as azelastine helps, but an intranasal steroid is the most effective single treatment for persistent blockage)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Nasal saline (Saline helps a little but is less effective than a nasal steroid)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Oral decongestant for months (Prolonged decongestants cause cardiovascular side effects and do not treat allergic inflammation)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Oral steroid (Oral steroids are only for short rescue courses, such as before exams)
x: An intranasal antihistamine such as azelastine helps, but an intranasal steroid is the most effective single treatment for persistent blockage.
Saline helps a little but is less effective than a nasal steroid.
Prolonged decongestants cause cardiovascular side effects and do not treat allergic inflammation
Oral steroids are only for short rescue courses, such as before exams.

hq_q.s: A 38 year old woman presents with severe, constant bilateral nasal blockage. Six weeks ago she developed a viral upper respiratory tract infection and began using an over-the-counter xylometazoline nasal spray five times daily. She reports that each dose now clears her nose for less than an hour before worse congestion returns. Anterior rhinoscopy shows beefy-red, boggy inferior turbinates with no nasal polyps and a central septum.
hq_q.w: Rhinitis medicamentosa is rebound nasal congestion caused by prolonged use (typically beyond 5 to 7 days) of topical alpha-adrenergic decongestants such as xylometazoline or oxymetazoline. Management involves stopping the decongestant spray and using an intranasal corticosteroid.
hq_q.f: Bilateral pale insensate nasal masses with anosmia and aspirin-sensitive asthma -> eosinophilic nasal polyposis.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most likely diagnosis?

c: xylometazoline nasal spray five times daily
clears her nose for less than an hour
tm.m: Prolonged topical alpha-agonist use downregulates mucosal alpha-adrenoceptors, causing rebound vasodilation and turbinate oedema when the drug wears off.
tm.g: Rebound nasal congestion with beefy-red turbinates after prolonged topical decongestant use -> Rhinitis medicamentosa
f: seasonal sneezing, watery rhinorrhoea, itchy eyes and pale boggy turbinates triggered by grass pollen
mucopurulent anterior and posterior nasal discharge with facial pain lasting over 12 weeks
lifelong unilateral nasal airflow obstruction following nasal trauma with visible septal deflection
bilateral pale insensate grape-like masses in the nasal cavity with anosmia and late-onset asthma
x: Allergic rhinitis causes paroxysmal sneezing, watery rhinorrhoea, nasal itch and pale bluish boggy turbinates rather than beefy-red rebound congestion from sympathomimetic overuse.
Chronic rhinosinusitis causes mucopurulent nasal discharge, facial pressure and hyposmia lasting over 12 weeks rather than tachyphylaxis to topical decongestants.
A deviated septum causes fixed, predominantly unilateral mechanical nasal obstruction and is excluded by the central septum on rhinoscopy.
Nasal polyps appear as pale, grey, mobile, insensate grape-like masses in the middle meatus rather than erythematous engorged inferior turbinates.

hq_q.s: A 17 year old student has severe hay fever with streaming eyes and nose. She has important exams in 2 weeks. She already uses an intranasal corticosteroid and an oral antihistamine correctly, but her symptoms continue.
o: A short course of oral prednisolone
hq_q.w: A short course of oral steroid can be used for important events. Depot injections are not recommended. Immunotherapy takes months to start working.
hq_q.f: Severe yearly symptoms despite treatment → refer for allergen immunotherapy.
hq_q.ql: Which is the most appropriate additional treatment?

c: uses an intranasal corticosteroid and an oral antihistamine correctly
tm.m: A short oral steroid course controls symptoms for an important event
tm.g: Severe hay fever before exams despite treatment: a short course of oral prednisolone
f: the presentation instead showed features specific to Immunotherapy started 1 week before (Allergen immunotherapy must be initiated months before the pollen season begins)
the presentation instead showed features specific to Intramuscular depot steroid as routine (Depot triamcinolone injections are not recommended due to prolonged systemic adverse effects)

the presentation instead showed features specific to Montelukast at night (Montelukast has a small effect on rhinitis and carries a neuropsychiatric warning; it is not the short-term rescue before exams)
a fit woman with no major illness
x: Allergen immunotherapy must be initiated months before the pollen season begins
Depot triamcinolone injections are not recommended due to prolonged systemic adverse effects
Montelukast has a small effect on rhinitis and carries a neuropsychiatric warning; it is not the short-term rescue before exams.
Ruled out here: requires a fit woman with no major illness, whereas this patient has important exams in 2 weeks, uses an intranasal corticosteroid and an oral antihistamine correctly.

hq_q.s: A 72 year old woman is admitted with a 2-day history of profuse watery diarrhoea and vomiting. She takes ramipril 10 mg daily. Pulse rate is 98 bpm and BP 102/64 mmHg. Her baseline serum creatinine 3 months ago was 80 µmol/L (60–120). Today her serum creatinine is 200 µmol/L, and her catheter urine output over 8 hours averages 0.6 mL/kg/hour.
hq_q.w: Under KDIGO criteria, AKI stage 1 is a creatinine rise to 1.5–1.9x baseline, stage 2 is 2.0–2.9x baseline, and stage 3 is >=3.0x baseline or >=354 µmol/L. A rise from 80 to 200 µmol/L is 2.5x baseline (stage 2).
hq_q.f: Serum creatinine rising from 80 µmol/L to 260 µmol/L (>3x baseline) -> AKI stage 3.
hq_q.ql: According to KDIGO criteria, which stage of acute kidney injury does she have?

c: Today her serum creatinine is 200 µmol/L
tm.m: A serum creatinine 2.5 times baseline (between 2.0 and 2.9 times baseline) defines KDIGO AKI stage 2.
tm.g: Creatinine 2.0–2.9x baseline (200 vs 80 µmol/L) -> AKI stage 2
f: serum creatinine rising from 80 µmol/L at baseline to 136 µmol/L during acute dehydration
serum creatinine rising from 80 µmol/L at baseline to 265 µmol/L with anuria for 12 hours
stable eGFR of 36 mL/min/1.73 m² persisting across repeat blood tests over 6 months
sustained eGFR of 22 mL/min/1.73 m² documented over 12 months in diabetic nephropathy
x: AKI stage 1 is defined by a creatinine rise to 1.5–1.9 times baseline (120–152 µmol/L here) or >=26.5 µmol/L within 48 hours.
AKI stage 3 requires a creatinine rise to >=3.0 times baseline (>=240 µmol/L here), an absolute creatinine >=354 µmol/L, or initiation of renal replacement therapy.
Her baseline creatinine was normal (80 µmol/L) 3 months ago and deteriorated acutely over 2 days of gastroenteritis, indicating AKI rather than stable CKD.
CKD stage 4 denotes chronic kidney disease with a sustained eGFR of 15–29 mL/min/1.73 m² for over 3 months, not an acute 2-day rise.

hq_q.s:
A 68 year old man has had vomiting and diarrhoea for 3 days and has acute kidney injury. His creatinine has risen from 90 to 180 µmol/L.
Pulse rate 108 bpm, BP 98/60 mmHg. His mucous membranes are dry.
Urine sodium 10 mmol/L. Urine osmolality 650 mOsm/kg. Urinalysis is bland.
hq_q.w: In pre-renal AKI, the kidneys hold sodium hard, so urine sodium is low and urine is concentrated. ATN gives high urine sodium.
hq_q.f: Urine sodium 60 with granular casts → acute tubular necrosis.
hq_q.ql: Which type of acute kidney injury is most likely?

tm.m: Underperfused but healthy kidneys hold on to sodium and concentrate urine
tm.g: Low urine sodium with concentrated urine and a bland sediment is pre-renal AKI
f: urine sodium of 60 with muddy brown casts
AKI with blood and protein in the urine and low complement
the presentation instead showed features specific to Interstitial nephritis (Interstitial nephritis follows a new drug with rash and eosinophils, not vomiting and diarrhoea)
hydronephrosis on ultrasound
x: Ruled out here: requires urine sodium of 60 with muddy brown casts, whereas this patient has Urine sodium 10, Urine osmolality 650.
Ruled out here: requires AKI with blood and protein in the urine and low complement, whereas this patient has Urine sodium 10, Urine osmolality 650.
Interstitial nephritis follows a new drug with rash and eosinophils, not vomiting and diarrhoea.
Ruled out here: requires hydronephrosis on ultrasound, whereas this patient has Urine sodium 10, Urine osmolality 650.

hq_q.s: A 58 year old woman started oral omeprazole 20 mg daily 10 days ago for dyspepsia. She presents with a 3-day history of fever, arthralgia and an itchy rash. Temperature is 37.9°C, pulse 86 bpm and BP 128/76 mmHg. A maculopapular eruption covers her trunk. Serum creatinine is 212 µmol/L (baseline 72 µmol/L), eosinophils are 1.1 x 10⁹/L (0.04–0.4) and urine microscopy shows sterile pyuria and eosinophiluria.
hq_q.w: Drug-induced acute interstitial nephritis is a T-cell-mediated hypersensitivity reaction within the renal interstitium, classically triggered 7 to 14 days after starting proton pump inhibitors, NSAIDs or penicillins, presenting with AKI, fever, rash, peripheral eosinophilia and sterile pyuria.
